Join us at Crowe and embark on a career where you can help shape the future of our industry.
Job Description:
Microsoft Security Practice Leader / Solution Architect
Job Summary
Crowe is seeking an experienced Microsoft Security Practice Leader / Solution Architect to help build and grow our emerging Microsoft Security practice. This role will lead enterprise security architecture and transformation engagements, advise senior client executives, and develop scalable Microsoft security solutions that help organizations modernize their security environments, protect identities and data, and strengthen cloud and AI security.
The ideal candidate combines deep Microsoft security architecture expertise with hands-on implementation experience, strong consulting delivery leadership, and the ability to build and develop high-performing teams.
This is a player-coach leadership role responsible for solution architecture, engagement delivery, client outcomes, and practice development. The successful candidate will work directly with CISOs, CIOs, and other executive stakeholders while helping establish reusable methodologies, service offerings, and a scalable US/India delivery model.
Key Responsibilities
Lead complex Microsoft security architecture, implementation, and transformation engagements for enterprise clients, ensuring technical quality, project delivery, and measurable business outcomes.
Serve as a trusted advisor to CISOs, CIOs, and other senior executives on cybersecurity strategy, architecture modernization, security platform consolidation, and technology investment decisions.
Design and implement integrated Zero Trust security architectures across Microsoft 365, Azure, on-premises, hybrid, and multicloud environments.
Conduct enterprise security architecture assessments, identify gaps and opportunities, and develop strategic roadmaps for security modernization and transformation.
Translate cybersecurity risks and technical findings into actionable business cases, investment priorities, licensing strategies, migration plans, operating models, and measurable outcomes.
Provide architecture and delivery leadership across Microsoft security technologies, including Microsoft Sentinel, Defender XDR, Entra, Purview, Defender for Cloud, Intune, Security Copilot, and Azure Logic Apps.
Lead security integration and transformation initiatives involving third-party SIEM, endpoint, identity, email-security, data-security, vulnerability-management, and cloud platforms.
Oversee engagement scope, technical solution design, implementation quality, project execution, and client deliverables.
Develop reusable intellectual property, including reference architectures, implementation methodologies, configuration standards, detection content, automation playbooks, and estimating models.
Recruit, manage, mentor, and develop security engineers, architects, and solution specialists across US and India delivery teams.
Establish technical standards, delivery processes, knowledge-sharing practices, and quality assurance methodologies to support consistent and scalable client delivery.
Collaborate with Microsoft's alliance organization to strengthen partner relationships, support certification initiatives, participate in partner programs, and identify client expansion opportunities.
Support practice growth through solution development, client pursuits, thought leadership, and the creation of repeatable consulting and managed-engineering services.
Balance client delivery responsibilities with practice development, team leadership, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Required Qualifications
12+ years of experience in cybersecurity, technology consulting, security engineering, or related disciplines, including substantial experience designing, implementing, or advising on Microsoft security technologies.
Demonstrated experience in enterprise security architecture, solution architecture, or technical program leadership, including leading complex security implementations and transformation programs.
Architecture-level expertise across the major Microsoft security product families, with hands-on implementation depth in at least three security domains, such as identity security, security operations, data protection, cloud security, AI security, or security architecture.
Strong experience designing integrated Microsoft security architectures across Microsoft 365, Azure, hybrid, on-premises, and multicloud environments.
Advanced knowledge of Zero Trust architecture, threat detection and response, identity and privileged access management, data protection, vulnerability management, cloud security, and security operations.
Experience with Microsoft security technologies such as Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Security Copilot, and related solutions.
Understanding of Microsoft security platform integrations with third-party technologies, including SIEM, endpoint security, identity management, email security, cloud security, and vulnerability management platforms.
Demonstrated experience leading enterprise consulting engagements, managing technical delivery, and advising executive stakeholders, including CISOs and CIOs.
Formal people-management experience, including recruiting, coaching, developing, and leading cross-functional or geographically distributed technical teams.
Ability to translate complex cybersecurity challenges into practical technical solutions, implementation roadmaps, and business-focused recommendations.
Strong consulting, stakeholder-management, problem-solving, and leadership skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication, executive presentation, facilitation, coaching, and conflict-resolution skills.
Ability to operate effectively in a growing practice while balancing client delivery, solution development, and team leadership responsibilities.
Preferred Qualifications
Active Microsoft security certification. Candidates without an active certification should be prepared to obtain one within 90 days of joining.
Microsoft Certified: Cybersecurity Architect Expert (SC-100), or willingness to obtain the certification within six months of joining.
Additional Microsoft security certifications such as SC-200, SC-300, SC-401, or SC-500.
Experience with Microsoft security platform consolidation, migration, and replacement of competing security technologies.
Experience integrating Microsoft security solutions with third-party platforms such as Splunk, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, CyberArk, Okta, Proofpoint, Zscaler, Netskope, Tenable, Rapid7, AWS, or Google Cloud.
Industry experience supporting financial services, banking, insurance, manufacturing, consumer products, retail, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, or medical devices organizations.
Experience supporting regulated organizations and collaborating with legal, privacy, compliance, audit, and risk stakeholders.
Established relationships within Microsoft, its field organization, partner ecosystem, or enterprise client accounts.
Experience developing consulting methodologies, reusable technical assets, managed-engineering services, or scalable delivery models.
Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field; an advanced degree is a plus.
Working Expectations
Willingness to travel approximately 20%–30% for client meetings, executive workshops, planning sessions, and team events.
Ability to maintain regular working-hour overlap with India-based colleagues approximately two to three days per week.
Flexibility to participate occasionally in after-hours activities related to cybersecurity incidents, production deployments, or global delivery requirements.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial consulting environment where service offerings, processes, and team structures are continuing to evolve.
What Success Looks Like
Successful candidates will help establish and grow Crowe's Microsoft Security practice by delivering complex enterprise security transformations, developing trusted executive client relationships, and building high-performing technical teams.
Within the first year, they will contribute to launching priority Microsoft security offerings, establishing repeatable architecture and delivery standards, developing reusable frameworks and methodologies, supporting new client opportunities, and strengthening Microsoft's alliance relationship.
They will also help build a scalable US/India delivery model while balancing billable client engagements, practice development, and team leadership responsibilities.
We expect the candidate to uphold Crowe’s values of Care, Trust, Courage, and Stewardship. These values define who we are. We expect all of our people to act ethically and with integrity at all times.

Job Summary
Crowe is seeking an experienced Microsoft Security Engineer to join our growing Microsoft Security practice. This role will support enterprise clients in modernizing and strengthening their cybersecurity environments through the implementation, configuration, and optimization of Microsoft security technologies.
The ideal candidate brings strong hands-on technical expertise in at least two core Microsoft security platforms, particularly Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft Sentinel, along with a passion for solving complex security challenges and delivering practical client solutions.
This is a hands-on technical delivery role focused on implementing security architectures, configuring and tuning security controls, troubleshooting technical issues, and supporting client engagements. The successful candidate will collaborate with security architects, engagement leaders, and other engineers to translate solution designs into effective, production-ready security capabilities.
Key Responsibilities
Implement, configure, and optimize Microsoft security solutions, including Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft Sentinel, based on established security architectures and client requirements.
Deploy and manage data governance and protection controls, including sensitivity labels, data loss prevention (DLP) policies, and insider risk management capabilities.
Configure identity and access management controls, including conditional access policies, identity governance workflows, and related Microsoft Entra security features.
Develop, implement, and tune Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules, workbooks, detection content, and automated response playbooks.
Build and refine security detection logic, correlation rules, and response automation to reduce false positives and improve threat detection and response capabilities.
Execute technical implementation plans, document configurations, troubleshoot deployment issues, and support security solution rollouts across client environments.
Participate in security architecture and design reviews, providing technical implementation insights and recommendations to architects and engagement leaders.
Support integration of Microsoft security solutions with third-party security technologies, including SIEM, endpoint protection, identity management, email security, data protection, vulnerability management, and cloud platforms.
Develop and maintain reusable technical assets, including configuration standards, implementation guides, detection content libraries, automation scripts, and technical runbooks.
Assist clients with solution adoption through technical documentation, knowledge transfer, and training on implemented security capabilities.
Collaborate with security architects, engagement leads, and engineering teams to ensure technical solutions meet client requirements and delivery standards.
Stay current with Microsoft security product updates, emerging capabilities, and industry best practices, sharing knowledge and recommendations with the broader team.
Required Qualifications
6+ years of experience in cybersecurity, information technology, security engineering, or related technical disciplines.
Demonstrated hands-on implementation and configuration experience with at least two of the following Microsoft security platforms: Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft Sentinel.
Experience independently configuring, deploying, tuning, and troubleshooting Microsoft security capabilities in enterprise environments.
Experience implementing data protection controls such as DLP policies, sensitivity labeling, and data governance capabilities within Microsoft Purview, where applicable to the candidate's specialization.
Experience configuring identity and access management controls, including conditional access policies and identity governance workflows within Microsoft Entra, where applicable.
Experience developing and tuning security analytics rules, detection logic, workbooks, and automation playbooks within Microsoft Sentinel, where applicable.
Working knowledge of core cybersecurity principles, including Zero Trust architecture, identity and access management, data protection, security operations, and incident response.
Understanding of Microsoft security integrations with enterprise security infrastructure and third-party security technologies.
Strong technical troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify configuration issues and implement effective solutions.
Experience documenting technical configurations, implementation procedures, and security recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with client technical teams and internal stakeholders.
Ability to work independently on assigned technical activities while collaborating with security architects, engagement leaders, and other engineering professionals.
Preferred Qualifications
Active Microsoft security certification such as SC-200, SC-300, SC-400, SC-401, or comparable credentials. Candidates without an active certification should be prepared to obtain one within 90 days of joining.
Hands-on implementation experience across all three core Microsoft security platforms: Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft Sentinel.
Familiarity with additional Microsoft security technologies, including Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Security Copilot, and Azure Logic Apps.
Experience integrating Microsoft security solutions with third-party platforms such as Splunk, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, CyberArk, Okta, Proofpoint, Zscaler, Netskope, Tenable, Rapid7, AWS, or Google Cloud.
Previous experience working in cybersecurity consulting, managed services, professional services, or other client-facing technical delivery environments.
Experience supporting regulated organizations or industries such as financial services, insurance, manufacturing, retail, or life sciences.
Proficiency with PowerShell, Kusto Query Language (KQL), Azure Logic Apps, or similar scripting and automation technologies.
Experience developing reusable technical documentation, implementation standards, security automation, or detection engineering content.
Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on professional experience.
Working Expectations
Willingness to travel approximately 10%–20% for client meetings, implementation activities, and team events.
Flexibility to participate occasionally in after-hours activities related to security incidents, production deployments, or scheduled maintenance windows.
Ability to collaborate effectively with security architects, engagement leaders, and geographically distributed engineering teams.
Ability to operate in a growing consulting practice where service offerings, technical standards, processes, and team structures continue to evolve.
What Success Looks Like
Successful candidates will demonstrate the ability to independently implement, configure, and optimize Microsoft security technologies while delivering reliable, high-quality solutions for enterprise clients.
Within the first six months, they will become proficient in client environments, take ownership of configuration and tuning activities, and establish themselves as a dependable technical resource in at least one Microsoft security platform.
Over the first year, they will expand their expertise across additional Microsoft security technologies, contribute to reusable implementation assets and automation, strengthen client delivery capabilities, and build the technical foundation for future advancement into senior engineering, architecture, or leadership positions.

People who thrive here are proactive, resourceful, and comfortable with ambiguity - taking initiative, bringing solutions, and following through as we grow.
Our Retailer Success team works closely with Retail Partners, Advertisers, Operations, and Engineering to support campaign execution, deliver actionable insights, and build strong partner relationships.
About the Role
As an Account Manager, Retailer Success, you will manage day-to-day retailer relationships and help partners grow adoption of our platform and scale their advertising businesses. You’ll support campaigns from planning and launch through reporting and optimization, while also coordinating go-to-market activities, gathering and tracking product roadmap requests, and triaging escalations. You’ll work closely with Ad Ops, Product, and Engineering to address retailer needs, resolve issues, and keep key initiatives moving forward.

title: Product Commercialization Engineer
description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY:
The Product Commercialization Engineer will get to work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, leading the scale-up and commercialization of adhesive, coating, and polymer technologies from laboratory development to full-scale manufacturing. This hands-on role partners with R&D, Operations, Engineering, Quality, EHS, Procurement, and Supply Chain to solve scale-up challenges and ensure products are manufactured safely, reliably, and cost-effectively across epoxy, acrylic/methacrylate, polyurethane, and hybrid polymer systems. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of driving innovation and growth for a division within a market-leading, Fortune 200 organization!
ITW BUSINESS MODEL & CULTURE
We have an environment shaped by our decentralized, entrepreneurial culture that brings our exciting ideas to life.  Our people thrive in our “flexibility within the framework” approach.
We are committed to providing you with growth and development opportunities that maximize your unique potential.
Our culture empowers you to think and act like a business owner – we want your entrepreneurial spirit to thrive!
Be a part of One ITW/One Team, where everyone’s contribution matters in our quest to achieve our full potential.
We live by our Core Values: simplicity, sharing risk, integrity, respect, and trust.
YOU MIGHT LIKE THIS JOB IF YOU ARE...
Are an entrepreneurial self-starter. You take initiative and ownership of your surroundings and constantly seek to find ways to improve.
Thrive in a fast-paced environment that keeps you on your toes – you love a good challenge, meeting aggressive deadlines, and can stay calm under pressure.
Have a passion for innovation and creating new technologies to solve customer pain points and market applicability.
Are resilient. You enjoy finding solutions to complex challenges and do so with poise and resolve.
Can work well with cross functional teams and lead by example. You have strong communication skills and the ability to influence without authority.
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Product Commercialization & Scale-Up
Lead commercialization and scale-up of new adhesive, coating, and polymer products from lab to full-scale manufacturing.
Develop robust, reproducible, and scalable manufacturing processes using chemical engineering principles and process science.
Identify and mitigate scale-up risks related to mixing, reaction control, heat transfer, equipment capability, and process variability.
Define operating windows and critical process parameters to ensure quality, consistency, and manufacturability.
Manufacturing & Process Improvement
Serve as a technical expert in polymer chemistry, process control, mixing, manufacturability, and raw material interactions.
Drive process improvements that enhance safety, quality, throughput, cost efficiency, and waste reduction while maintaining product performance.
Lead manufacturing troubleshooting, root-cause investigations, and resolution of batch variability and scale-dependent performance issues.
Apply DOE, statistical analysis, and structured problem-solving tools to optimize processes and resolve manufacturing challenges.
Change Management & Process Technology
Lead evaluation, validation, and implementation of raw material, process, equipment, and manufacturing site changes, including alternative and second-source materials.
Identify, evaluate, and implement new manufacturing technologies, process controls, equipment, and analytical tools that support commercialization and operational excellence.
Support equipment qualification, process commissioning, manufacturing start-ups, and production readiness activities.
Safety, Quality & Leadership
Provide technical leadership across R&D, Operations, Quality, EHS, Supply Chain, suppliers, and external partners to deliver safe, compliant, cost-effective, and successful product commercialization.
Promote, support, and adhere to all safety, environmental and quality related policies and procedures .
QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, & COMPETENCIES:
B.S. in Chemical Engineering or a closely related engineering discipline.
Minimum 5 years of experience in product/process scale-up and commercialization within a chemical manufacturing environment, including transfer from laboratory through pilot to commercial production.
Demonstrated experience bridging R&D/product development and manufacturing operations, including technology transfer and support of production scale-up between sites. Demonstrated track record of successfully commercializing new products at industrial production scale.
Strong knowledge of chemical engineering fundamentals, including mixing, heat transfer, mass transfer, reaction engineering, process control, and industrial manufacturing equipment/processes.
Proven ability to troubleshoot manufacturing and product-quality issues using structured problem-solving methods, including DOE, statistical analysis, process data analysis, and root-cause investigation; proficiency with tools such as JMP or Minitab preferred.
Demonstrated experience qualifying raw materials and alternate sources in incumbent commercial products.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across technical, operational, and manufacturing teams.
Experience preferred in the adhesives, coatings, sealants, specialty polymers, or formulated chemical products industries, primarily with epoxy, polyurethane, acrylic/methacrylate, and/or hybrid polymer chemistries.
Travel:  Ability to travel periodically to manufacturing facilities, suppliers, and partner locations within the United States. Occasional international travel may be required.

The salary for this role is $100,000.00 - $125,000.00. This is the range that we in good faith anticipate relying on when setting wages for this position. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and this range. This salary range may also be modified in the future.

description:
Job Description:
The Senior Buyer is a key supply chain leader responsible for driving procurement, supplier performance, inventory management, and continuous improvement initiatives within the Precision Welding Solutions Division. In this role you will partner closely with the Materials Manager, suppliers, engineering and cross-functional teams to ensure excellence in cost, quality and delivery.
You will provide leadership, develop talent and drive results across the Precision Welding Solutions Division.  The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, demonstrates strong negotiation and relationship building skills and can drive change through collaboration and influence.
How You Will Make an Impact:
Supply Chain & Procurement
Manage procurement activities, including sourcing, purchasing, inventory planning, and material flow.
Lead supplier negotiations involving pricing, contracts, delivery performance, and service levels.
Evaluate, select, and develop suppliers in partnership with the Materials Manager and engineering team.
Build collaborative supplier relationships while identifying opportunities for supplier consolidation and risk reduction.
Conduct supplier visits, audits, and performance reviews.
Manage supplier corrective action processes and ensure timely resolution of quality or delivery issues.
Monitor and communicate Market Rate of Demand (MRD) changes to suppliers
Cost & Inventory Management
Drive cost reduction, productivity, quality, delivery, and simplification initiatives.
Manage material price variance, inventory turns, and inventory optimization programs.
Track and document cost savings and cost avoidance projects.
Maintain inventory accuracy through cycle count oversight and inventory management practices.
Support inventory transition activities related to product launches, engineering changes, and product obsolescence.
Manage MOH and inactive inventory performance metrics.
Strategic Initiatives
Lead or support divisional materials and supply chain improvement projects.
Develop and implement materials strategies aligned with business objectives.
Actively participate in New Product Development (NPD) initiatives.
Partner daily with manufacturing, engineering, and other cross-functional teams to ensure material availability and operational continuity.
Champion and implement ITW business principles, including 80/20, Product Line Simplification, Market Rate of Demand (MRD), Empowerment, Trust, and Continuous Improvement.
Leadership & Talent Development
Provide leadership, coaching, and support to materials personnel and cross-functional teams.
Depending on organizational needs and candidate experience, the role may include direct supervision of materials personnel.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, improve efficiency, and develop organizational capabilities
How You Show Up:
Collaborative Leader – Builds strong relationships through effective leadership, communication and interpersonal skills.
Supplier Partnership – Builds and maintains supplier relationships while driving negotiation, quality, delivery and cost performance.
Ownership Mindset – Takes initiative to lead cost reduction, inventory management and new product development projects.
Results-Driven – Prioritizes effectively, approaches challenges analytically and follows through to achieve results.
Growth Mindset – Demonstrates a commitment to continuous learning, professional development and personal growth.
Qualifications:

Experience coaching, developing or leading teams either through direct supervision or cross-functional leadership

Miller Electric Mfg. LLC, is headquartered in Appleton, Wisconsin, and wholly owned by  Illinois Tool Works  (NYSE: ITW). Our tagline, “The Power of Blue®,” is inspired by the blue color of Miller equipment.

title: Analyst, EFT Trade Compliance and Operations (Bi-Lingual English/Spanish)
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position
The Analyst, EFT Trade Compliance and Operations is responsible for overseeing and
coordinating all international movements originating from the United States to destinations
worldwide, including but not limited to Mexico, Germany, Bulgaria, and Malaysia. The scope
includes equipment, service parts, repairs, upgrades, returns, loaners, demonstrations,
manufacturing-related tools, components, and materials. This role serves as the primary
coordinator for the end-to-end Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) process and as the
operational interface among engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, logistics,
customs brokers, suppliers, and trade compliance. The position owns shipment visibility,
status management, escalation handling, regulatory readiness, classification
governance, permit management, and export/import compliance from submission through
U.S. export and destination-country import. It ensures products are properly classified,
registered, documented, and compliance-ready before shipment approval.
Essential Job Duties
 Manage end-to-end international movements of capital equipment, repairs, returns,
demonstration units, components, service parts, manufacturing-related tools, and
materials from the United States to countries worldwide
 Serve as the primary point of contact for international outbound movements from the
United States and related returns, and lead cross-functional escalation calls for critical
shipments.
 Manage active Shipment Authorization Form (SAF) requests, monitor shipment
milestones and readiness, and serve as the primary owner of the SAF Helpline Zoom
Channel.
 Provide shipment status updates to engineers and project teams, track open issues,
and ensure timely resolution.
 Coordinate with customs brokers, freight forwarders, and logistics providers to
support timely U.S. export and destination-country import clearance and resolve holds,
delays, documentation issues, and classification discrepancies.
 Manage U.S. export and destination-country tariff classification activities.
 Partner with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, suppliers, and
trade compliance to obtain and evaluate technical information required for classification
and country of origin determinations.
 Review engineering drawings, Bills of Materials, product specifications,
materials, component information, and product functionality to support HTS, Schedule
B, ECCN, and country of origin determinations.
 Verify completion of classification, country of origin documentation, FTA eligibility, metal
certificates, permit or license approvals, and customs documentation readiness.
 Evaluate destination-country import requirements, including permits, product
registrations, labeling or conformity requirements, special regulations, and customs
restrictions.
 Coordinate product data required for applicable customs, inventory control, and trade
compliance systems.
 Ensure products are compliance-ready before shipment authorization and support
inventory registration requirements and customs record maintenance.
 Ensure accurate tracking of exported, imported, transformed, returned, scrapped, and
transferred goods.
 Prepare, review, and validate commercial invoices, export filings, permits, licenses,
certificates, temporary import/export documents, and country-specific customs
declarations.
 Ensure compliance with U.S. export requirements, destination-country import
regulations, applicable trade laws, sanctions and restricted-party requirements, and
company policies.
 Maintain complete, audit-ready trade records and ensure proper export documentation,
recordkeeping, and regulatory compliance.
 Support engineering, manufacturing, service, and supply chain teams with global trade
compliance requirements.
 Support tariff and export classification, country of origin determinations, and trade
program utilization.
 Participate in internal audits and government compliance reviews, perform trade
compliance due diligence and transaction reviews, and support audits and
investigations.
 Identify compliance risks, implement corrective actions, and define requirements for
new shipment types and destination countries.
 Develop and maintain SOPs, procedures, work instructions, playbooks, knowledge
repositories, and classification databases.
 Identify process improvement and automation opportunities and support
implementation of global trade technology solutions.
 Maintain SAF tracking dashboards and monitor SLA performance; report shipment
aging, cycle times, backlog, and escalation metrics.
 Perform other duties, tasks, and special projects as assigned.
Required Skills and Experience
 Minimum 5 years of experience in:
• U.S.-Mexico cross-border operations
• Customs compliance
• Import/export operations
• IMMEX program administration
 Fluent in English and Spanish (written and verbal).
 Experience preparing customs documentation and supporting customs audits.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Advanced Excel and ERP system experience.
Preferred Skills and Experience
 Experience in the medical device, healthcare, pharmaceutical, or highly regulated
manufacturing industry.
 Experience with FDA-regulated products.
 Knowledge of USMCA and other free trade agreement requirements.
 Experience with SAP, GTS, Annex 24 software, or other customs compliance systems.
 Customs certifications or trade compliance credentials are a plus.
 Knowledge of:
• IMMEX Program
• Annex 24
• Annex 30
• U.S. Import Compliance
• U.S. Export Compliance
• Customs broker management
• Temporary import/export programs
Education & Training
 Bachelor's degree in engineering, international trade, customs administration, supply
chain, business, logistics, or a related field.
Working Conditions
Normal office conditions.
Travel required (<10%) – both domestic and international.

Compensation will be based primarily on the job level at which the role is filled and the

Position Overview
The Upstream Reimbursement Strategist is the architect of the organization’s long-range reimbursement and market access strategy across the U.S. product portfolio. This person is responsible for generating all strategies for all upstream programs and dovetailing those strategies with global market access for ex-U.S. projects. This role is the closest link to the clinical development team and serves as the primary strategic interface with HEOR, regulatory affairs, and health policy stakeholders.
Responsible for evidence generation strategy, CPT/HCPCS code pathway design, CMS payment policy analysis, and the global coordination of evidence that feeds both upstream regulatory submissions and downstream field execution tools. This person shapes the narrative for why a product deserves reimbursement and builds the data package to support it.
Core Responsibilities
CPT/HCPCS Code Strategy: Lead the strategy for new code applications, Category III code conversions, and descriptor modifications. Manage engagement with AMA CPT Editorial Panel, RUC, and HCPCS workgroups.
CMS Payment Policy Analysis: Conduct ongoing analysis of OPPS, PFS, and ASC payment policy. Prepare and submit CMS comment letters during rulemaking cycles. Monitor NT-APC, pass-through, and device payment category developments.
Global Evidence Coordination: Serve as the connective tissue between U.S. evidence needs and global HEOR and OUS markets. Dovetail U.S. upstream strategies with global market access to ensure alignment on ex-U.S. projects. Ensure evidence generation is sequenced to serve both U.S. regulatory/payer needs and ex-U.S. HTA submissions, coordinating timing and deliverables across jurisdictions.
Coverage & Reimbursement Strategy: Generate and own the reimbursement strategy for all upstream programs across the full product portfolio. Develop and maintain the strategic reimbursement roadmap from early pipeline through commercialization, including target product profiles (TPPs) and core value dossiers (CVDs) for pipeline assets. Identify coverage gaps, analyze competitive reimbursement positioning, recommend pathway strategies, and ensure strategic continuity as products progress through development milestones.
U.S. Value Plan Implementation Support: Play a supporting role to HEOR in ensuring the U.S. Market Access team has secured the database resources required to execute strategy and implement the recommendations set out in the U.S. Value Plan.
Competitive Intelligence: Monitor competitor reimbursement strategies, code applications, pass-through approvals, and coverage determinations. Translate competitive intelligence into actionable strategic recommendations.
Product Positioning & Message Alignment: Serve as the primary owner of product positioning in coordination with select downstream stakeholders, ensuring messaging is consistent across other stakeholders in the organization — particularly when producing publications such as burden of illness, cost-utility, and budget impact analyses.
Market Access Research: Lead market access research to support value messaging, including claims analyses and — where needed — coordination of payer interviews, provider interviews, and other primary research.
Shared Midstream Responsibility: Contribute to code acquisition execution, pre-launch payer engagement planning, and payment policy implementation activities in partnership with the Mid/Downstream Tactician.
Required
Health policy degree or similar
3-8+ years of progressive experience in medical device market access, health economics, reimbursement strategy, or related field (for manager level, 3+)
Deep working knowledge of CMS OPPS/PFS/ASC payment systems, APC mechanics, and facility payment methodology
Experience with CPT, , AMA Editorial Panel processes, and HCPCS coding pathways
Strong analytical skills with experience interpreting claims data, cost reports, and CMS rulemaking documents
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate complex policy into strategic recommendations
Ability to work cross-functionally with clinical, regulatory, HEOR, and commercial teams
Preferred
Advanced degree (MPH, MBA, or equivalent; PhD or PharmD also welcome)
Familiarity with healthcare data platforms
Familiarity with HEOR models

This position is a dynamic technical systems focused role that requires strong communication, problem solving, cross functional teamwork and ability to present and drive continuous improvement to processes, products, and systems.  Your primary responsibilities will include:
Create, maintain, and improve manufacturing processes and methods to perform failure analysis of returned parts, identifying root causes of failed products.

Minimum 5 years experience as design or manufacturing engineer supporting product with significant electromechanical content.
Sense of curiosity and a willingness to always dig deeper.
Ability to read electronic and mechanical schematics, assembly, and fabrication drawings.  Execute testing and data collection using Linux, Matlab, and other software toolsets.
Strong skills in problem solving and using Minitab/JMP, Python, SQL, Tableau and/or other SW tools for data analysis to identify root cause and drive corrective actions.

Ability to lift, and carry parts weighing up to 40 lbs

“Self-starter” attitude and comfort in a hands-on environment, where he/she can demonstrate an ability to work with other engineers to influence product and manufacturing design to improve reliability.
Experience in an ISO 13485, ISO 9001, or medical device manufacturing environment

Primary Function of Position
Services Technical Publications provides the foundation for every procedure performed on Intuitive's advanced medical devices by the global Field Service team. Our content is authored in DITA and delivered through guided workflows, which progressively discloses content for field service technicians install, maintain, and repair Intuitive systems.
In this role, you will combine expert editing skills with strategic thinking to develop and implement a comprehensive quality metrics program. You will work directly with technical writers, product teams, and stakeholders to ensure that hardware and software documentation meets our highest standards for clarity, accuracy, consistency, and usability within guided, step-by-step workflows.
As an individual contributor with significant influence and authority, your success will be measured by your ability to drive quality improvements and positive outcomes through collaboration, coaching, and strategic program development—not through direct management, but through leadership and expertise.
Essential Job Duties
Edit hardware and software technical documentation for clarity, accuracy, consistency, voice, tone, and usability. Champion minimalist, task-based writing principles to ensure content serves the immediate needs of field service technicians. Work directly with authors and SMEs to improve content quality across the publication lifecycle.
Make edits directly in IXIA, our component content management system, collaborating with technical writers and subject matter experts through the review workflow to implement changes efficiently. Comfort navigating the system and driving content improvements end-to-end.
Develop and own a quality metrics program that establishes baselines, identifies improvement opportunities, and measures impact. Use data-driven insights to guide editorial strategy and demonstrate ROI of editing services.
Design and implement best practices for technical content quality. Create scalable processes, guidelines, and checklists that enable teams to self-serve and maintain consistency without bottlenecking editorial review.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams—including product, UX, localization, and publishing—to align on quality standards and resolve editorial challenges.

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent
7+ years of professional editing experience in technical communications, with demonstrated expertise editing DITA-authored content for both hardware and software products.
Deep expertise in minimalist and task-based, topic-based authoring approaches. Demonstrated ability to coach authors on these principles and evaluate content for adherence to minimalist standards.
Proficiency with IXIA or similar component content management systems (CCMS). Ability to navigate the system, make edits directly, and move content through review workflows independently.
Experience developing or implementing editorial guidelines, style guides, or content quality standards. Comfort with creating scalable, repeatable processes.
Proficiency with quality assurance tools such as Acrolinx, Congree, Grammarly, or equivalent. Ability to evaluate tools and troubleshoot configuration issues.
Proven ability to communicate clearly and concisely, both in written and spoken formats. Skill in explaining complex editorial feedback in a way that educates rather than demoralizes.
Experience working with metrics, data collection, or quality measurement. Comfort with analyzing trends and using data to support recommendations.
Ability to influence and drive outcomes without direct authority. Success collaborating with subject matter experts, product teams, and writers who may not report to you.

Experience with medical device, surgical instrument, or other regulated/high-stakes technical documentation.
Familiarity with content management systems, publishing workflows, or localization processes.
Experience training or coaching other writers or editors.
Understanding of how DITA-authored content serves guided workflows with progressive disclosure, and how editing decisions impact both user experience and compliance.

description:

Primary Function of Position:
The Sr. Workday Solutions Architect, Compensation is responsible for the design, configuration, and continuous improvement of Workday Core Compensation and Advanced Compensation, along with the Core HCM foundation these solutions depend on, including Job Architecture, organizations, and position data.
Reporting to the Director, Workday Solutions, this role serves as the senior technical authority for compensation in Workday. The architect translates Total Rewards strategy and complex business requirements into scalable, compliant, and auditable solutions, covering pay structures, plan design, eligibility, and annual review cycles for merit, bonus, and stock.
This role works in close partnership with Total Rewards, HR Executives, Centers of Excellence (COEs), Finance, HR Business Leaders, and IT leadership to deliver accurate, reliable, and user-friendly compensation experiences for employees, managers, and compensation teams.
The successful candidate pairs deep Workday compensation expertise with a strong command of the HCM structures that drive it, and uses that combination to deliver design decisions that stand up to audit and scale with the business.
Key Responsibilities
Compensation Solution Architecture & Strategy
·      Own the end-to-end architecture for Workday Core and Advanced Compensation, ensuring designs align with Total Rewards strategy, enterprise standards, and business goals.
·      Lead requirements gathering, fit-gap analysis, and design workshops with Total Rewards, HR, Finance, and IT stakeholders.
·      Provide input to the Workday and HR technology roadmap, including compensation priorities, release adoption, and technical debt reduction.
·      Evaluate Workday semi-annual releases and recommend, plan, and manage the adoption of new compensation features.
Core Compensation
·      Design and maintain compensation structures, including grades, grade profiles, steps, salary ranges, and pay differentials by geography and job.
·      Configure compensation plans (salary, hourly, allowance, and other plan types), eligibility rules, and compensation packages.
·      Design and optimize compensation-related business processes, such as hire, promotion, transfer, and ad hoc compensation changes.
·      Manage compensation data integrity, including mass updates, range and structure changes, and effective-dated corrections.
Advanced Compensation
·      Architect and configure annual compensation review cycles for merit, bonus, and stock, including review events, worksheets, budgets, guidelines, and approval routing.
·      Design bonus, merit, and stock plans with complex eligibility, proration, target, and calculation logic using calculated fields and condition rules.
·      Build compensation review analytics, dashboards, and reports that give Total Rewards and business leaders visibility into budgets, spend, and outcomes.
·      Lead pre-cycle readiness, including data validation, security setup, testing, and manager and compensation partner enablement, and provide hypercare during active review cycles.
Core HCM Foundation & Job Architecture
·      Design and maintain Job Architecture, including job families, job profiles, job categories, and management levels, and align it with compensation grades and pay structures.
·      Ensure supervisory organizations, positions, locations, companies, and worker data are structured to support accurate compensation eligibility, review cycles, and reporting.
·      Own the intersection of HCM and Compensation business processes (e.g., job change, promotion, transfer, termination) and their effect on compensation.
·      Define domain and business process security policies, role-based access, and segregation of duties for sensitive compensation data.
·      Partner with HR Operations and Talent teams to govern job profile creation and changes so that data stays consistent and audit-ready.
Integrations, Data & Governance
·      Collaborate with IT on the design of compensation-related integrations, including feeds to payroll, finance, equity administration, and market data providers.
·      Partner with IT on integration implementation management, including requirements, data mapping, build and test coordination, deployment, and post go-live monitoring and support.
·      Lead data conversion, loading, and validation efforts for implementations, acquisitions, and major organizational changes.
·      Establish configuration standards, change management practices, and testing strategies, including regression testing and UAT.
·      Ensure compensation solutions meet audit, data privacy, and regulatory requirements, including Sarbanes-Oxley controls.
Delivery & Stakeholder Management
·      Build and execute detailed implementation plans, including discovery, design, QA/testing, deployment, and support.
·      Act as a point of escalation for complex compensation system issues and support troubleshooting with Workday, implementation partners, and other vendors.
·      Serve as a trusted advisor to Total Rewards and HR leaders, influencing decisions through data, collaboration, and measurable outcomes.
Leadership & Team Development
·      Mentor and coach solution architects and analysts, conducting design and configuration reviews to raise the quality of delivery.
·      Promote agile ways of working and strong cross-functional partnerships across HR, Finance, Technology, and business teams.
Skills, Experience, Education & Training
Minimum Qualifications:
·      Minimum 8+ years of hands-on Workday experience, including at least 5 years focused on Workday Compensation and at least 3 years in an architect or lead role.
·      Active Workday certifications in Workday Core Compensation and Workday Advanced Compensation .
·      Proven experience leading at least 2 full-lifecycle Workday implementations or major deployments that included Core and Advanced Compensation, including at least one annual compensation review cycle.
·      Deep expertise in Core HCM foundations that drive compensation, including Job Architecture (job families, job profiles, management levels), supervisory organizations, position management, and worker data.
·      Strong working knowledge of the Workday business process framework, security, calculated fields, condition rules, and reporting.
·      Experience collaborating with IT on the design and implementation of Workday integrations
·      Strong understanding of compensation concepts, including pay structures, merit cycles, bonus plans, equity, and market pricing.
·      Minimum bachelor’s degree in technology, business, human resources, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
·      Experience with a global/international company with employee populations across multiple regions.
·      Strong customer orientation and superb communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly with technical, functional, and executive audiences; strong personal and technical influencing skills.
·      Process orientation and technical project management skills; experience with multiple project methodologies, including Agile/iterative development, a plus.
·      Familiarity with US and global data privacy laws, GDPR, and Sarbanes-Oxley compliance.
Preferred Qualifications:
·      Active Workday HCM Core certification
·      Additional Workday certifications (e.g., Security, Benefits, Absence).
·      Experience with Workday release management and tenant strategy.
·      Experience working in a regulated industry such as healthcare or medical devices.
·      Comfortable operating in fast-changing environments and creating clarity out of ambiguity.

title: Sr. Workday Solutions Architect, HCM and Talent
description:

We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position:
The Sr. Workday Solutions Architect, HCM Core & Talent Management is responsible for the design, configuration, and continuous improvement of Workday Core HCM and Talent Management, including Onboarding and Performance Management, so that employees, managers, and HR teams have a seamless experience across the employee lifecycle.
Reporting to the Director, Workday Solutions, this role serves as the senior technical authority for Core HCM foundations and Talent Management processes in Workday. The architect translates business and HR requirements into scalable, secure, and user-friendly solutions, and sets the design standards that guide the broader team of solution architects and analysts.
This role works in close partnership with HR Executives, Talent and other Centers of Excellence (COEs), HR Business Leaders, and IT leadership to deliver reliable and intuitive HR experiences built on the Workday platform.
The successful candidate combines deep Workday expertise with strong stakeholder management and communication skills, turning business needs into well-architected solutions that deliver measurable employee, manager, and business outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
Solution Architecture & Strategy
·      Own the end-to-end architecture for Workday Core HCM and Talent Management, ensuring designs align with enterprise standards and business strategy.
·      Lead requirements gathering, fit-gap analysis, and design workshops with HR, Talent COE, and business stakeholders.
·      Provide input to the Workday and HR technology roadmap, including Talent priorities, release adoption, and technical debt reduction.
·      Evaluate Workday semi-annual releases and recommend, plan, and manage the adoption of new HCM and Talent features.
Core HCM
·      Architect and configure worker data, supervisory organizations, job architecture, staffing models, and position management.
·      Design and optimize business processes such as hire, transfer, promotion, termination, and leave.
·      Build and maintain calculated fields, custom reports, dashboards, and condition rules.
·      Maintain data integrity and effective-dated accuracy across HCM structures that drive Talent processes.
Onboarding
·      Design and configure Workday Onboarding, including onboarding templates, tasks, and checklists for new hires, rehires, and internal movers.
·      Partner with HR Operations, IT, and Facilities on pre-boarding and day-one workflows that create a consistent new hire and manager experience.
·      Configure onboarding documents, forms, and approvals, and ensure data flows accurately into downstream systems.
Performance Management
·      Architect and configure end-to-end performance review cycles, including review templates, sections, and questions, and cycle timing and eligibility.
·      Configure employee self-assessments, manager assessments, and feedback, including requested, given, and peer feedback.
·      Design rating models, calculation logic, and rating scales, and support calibration of ratings.
·      Configure the 9-box talent grid and calibration sessions, including performance and potential assessments and the related reporting and approvals.
·      Design and support the promotion nomination process, including nomination, review, approval routing, and hand-off to HCM and compensation processes.
·      Set up and manage goals, including organizational, team, and individual goals, alignment, and goal cascading.
·      Build Talent analytics and reports that give HR and business leaders visibility into completion, ratings distribution, and talent outcomes.
·      Lead pre-cycle readiness, including data validation, testing, and manager and employee communications, and provide hypercare during active review cycles.
Security & Role-Based Access
·      Define and maintain domain and business process security policies, role-based access, and segregation of duties for HCM and Talent Management roles.
·      Design role-based security for Talent roles such as employees, managers, HR Partners, Talent COE, and calibration participants, so that sensitive data like ratings and potential is visible only to the right audiences.
·      Partner with Security and Compliance on periodic access reviews, audit support, and remediation.
Integrations, Data & Governance
·      Collaborate with IT on the design of HCM and Talent integrations, including onboarding-related and talent data feeds.
·      Partner with IT on integration implementation management, including requirements, data mapping, build and test coordination, deployment, and post go-live monitoring and support.
·      Lead data conversion, loading, and validation efforts for implementations, acquisitions, and major organizational changes.
·      Establish configuration standards, change management practices, and testing strategies, including regression testing and UAT.
·      Ensure data accuracy, security, and privacy across HR systems and solutions, in line with audit and regulatory requirements.
Delivery & Stakeholder Management
·      Build and execute detailed implementation plans, including discovery, design, QA/testing, deployment, and support.
·      Act as a point of escalation for complex system issues and support troubleshooting with Workday, implementation partners, and other vendors.
·      Serve as a trusted advisor to HR and business leaders, communicating complex technical concepts clearly and influencing decisions through data, collaboration, and measurable outcomes.
Leadership & Team Development
·      Mentor and coach solution architects and analysts, conducting design and configuration reviews to raise the quality of delivery.
·      Promote agile ways of working and strong cross-functional partnerships across HR, Technology, and business teams.
Skills, Experience, Education & Training
Minimum Qualifications:
·      Minimum 8+ years of hands-on Workday experience, including at least 3 years in an architect or lead role.
·      Active Workday certifications in Workday HCM Core and Workday Talent Management .
·      Proven experience leading at least 2 full-lifecycle Workday implementations or major deployments that included Core HCM and Talent Management, including at least one full performance review cycle.
·      Deep expertise in Workday Onboarding and Performance Management, including self-assessments, manager assessments, feedback, ratings, 9-box calibration, promotion nominations, and goals.
·      Strong experience with role-based security in Workday, particularly for Talent Management roles, including domain and business process security policies.
·      Strong working knowledge of the Workday business process framework, calculated fields, condition rules, and reporting.
·      Experience collaborating with IT on the design and implementation of Workday integrations using EIB, Core Connectors, and/or Workday Studio.
·      Minimum bachelor’s degree in technology, business, human resources, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
·      Experience with a global/international company with employee populations across multiple regions.
·      Effective stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage and influence partners across the company, including senior-level leadership.
·      Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly with technical, functional, and executive audiences.
·      Process orientation and technical project management skills; experience with multiple project methodologies, including Agile/iterative development, a plus.
·      Familiarity with US and global data privacy laws, GDPR, and Sarbanes-Oxley compliance.
Preferred Qualifications:
·      Additional Workday certifications (e.g., Security, Reporting).
·      Experience with Workday Skills Cloud, Talent Optimization, or Workday Illuminate and other AI-enabled talent capabilities.
·      Experience with Workday release management and tenant strategy.
·      Experience working in a regulated industry such as healthcare or medical devices.
·      Comfortable operating in fast-changing environments and creating clarity out of ambiguity.

title: Principal HVDC Engineer, Grid Integration Engineering
description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future.
Invenergy follows a hybrid schedule, working in office Monday through Thursday and remotely on Fridays if work permits.
This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window.
Job Description
Role Scope and Interface
This role leads study scopes, technical reviews, issue resolution, and cross-functional coordination within Grid Integration Engineering. Interconnection & Grid Analysis retains formal submissions, process management, and agreement negotiations. OEMs and consultants execute contracted studies; Grid Modeling supports modeling and validation consistent with project-phase responsibilities. Engineering and Construction retain detailed implementation and field execution.
Responsibilities
HVDC Interconnection and GBX Cluster Studies
•    Lead the technical scope and coordination of HVDC interconnection studies with SPP’s Transmission Working Group (TWG), MISO, and AECI, including related affected-system studies and material modification assessments.
•    Manage GBX generation cluster studies, coordinating project and OEM data, model packages, study assumptions, consultant deliverables, technical comments, and dependencies with the HVDC interconnection workstreams.
•    Develop study scopes, case lists, schedules, and technical deliverables; manage consultants and coordinate inputs with the HVDC OEM, Interconnection & Grid Analysis, Grid Modeling, and project teams.
•    Oversee model sourcing, quality testing, validation, and cross-platform benchmarking. Maintain consistency of PSS/E and PSCAD models, plant configurations, control settings, and data across interconnection and OEM studies.
•    Review power flow, short-circuit, dynamic stability, and electromagnetic transient (EMT) results; resolve model deficiencies and study findings, and assess proposed mitigations with Interconnection & Grid Analysis and Engineering.
•    Translate final study outcomes and agreement obligations into the Design Basis for Grid Compliance and final interconnection-study model package, including accepted material modifications, for handoff to Engineering and Grid Modeling.
OEM System Design and Performance Verification
•    Lead Invenergy’s technical oversight of OEM system design studies, including main circuit parameters, equipment ratings, transient stress, insulation coordination, harmonics, and AC/DC system interactions.
•    Define and review DPS cases and acceptance criteria covering operating modes, AC/DC faults, recovery, grid strength, and control/protection interactions. Ensure findings are reflected in design, settings, and project models.
•    Lead owner-side planning and review of DPT and Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS)-based control and protection testing, including hardware-in-the-loop test scope, network representation, procedures, witnessing, results, and corrective-action closure.
•    Develop study, model, performance, and testing requirements for OEM and consultant contracts; evaluate technical deviations and maintain alignment between design studies, interconnection commitments, factory testing, and commissioning.
•    Coordinate with Procurement, Engineering, Protection and Controls, SCADA, Compliance, Regulatory Affairs, Operations, and project management. Communicate technical risks and recommendations to leadership, mentor engineers, and establish repeatable study-review practices.
Minimum Qualifications
•    Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or a related engineering discipline.
•    10+ years of relevant power-system engineering experience, including direct experience in HVDC system design, interconnection studies, or converter-system performance analysis.
•    Strong understanding of voltage-source converter HVDC systems, main circuit design, transient behavior, AC/DC interactions, and control and protection principles.
•    Experience performing or technically leading PSCAD/EMTDC and PSS/E studies, or equivalent simulation tools, including model validation and interpretation of study results.
•    Experience managing OEM or consultant study deliverables, technical specifications, interconnection requirements, and resolution of complex modeling or performance issues.
•    Ability to coordinate engineering efforts across teams and communicate technical recommendations and their cost, schedule, and compliance implications to engineering and business stakeholders.
•    Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.
Preferred Qualifications
•    Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering; Professional Engineer (PE) license or equivalent professional certification.
•    Experience with SPP TWG, MISO, AECI, affected-system studies, and generation cluster or material modification studies.
•    Experience with DPT, RTDS/RSCAD, hardware-in-the-loop testing, OEM control/protection systems, or HVDC factory testing and commissioning.

description:
Job Description:
Advertising & Promotions Finance Manager
At Mars, we believe pets make the world a better place, and behind our seven awesome brands is a significant investment in building brands pet parents love. The Advertising & Consumer Promotions Finance Manager (A&CP) gets a front-row seat to how we bring those brands to life, serving as the finance co-pilot for our A&CP investment.
From big brand campaigns to the investments that help us connect with pet parents every day, this role provides financial leadership across planning, forecasting, execution, close, and partnering , helping ensure every dollar works as hard as our brands do.
What are we looking for?
5+ years of Finance experience in Marketing Finance, Commercial Finance, FP&A, or Business Partnering
Strong capabilities in budgeting, forecasting, accruals, period close, and management reporting
Proven ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and translate financial data into business insights
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills required; Alteryx experience preferred
Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment with strong attention to detail
Demonstrated ability to manage ambiguity, drive accountability, and improve processes
What will be your key responsibilities?
Serve as the primary Finance partner for A&CP, collaborating with Marketing, Marketing Operations, PGT Finance, and agency partners
Provide financial guidance and challenge to support optimal investment decisions
Lead annual budgeting and forecasting activities, ensuring alignment to business priorities and financial commitments
Maintain visibility to A&CP investments, performance, risks, and opportunities
Deliver actionable insights and recommendations to business and Finance leadership
Own period-close activities, including expense recognition, accruals, variance analysis, and reporting integrity

title: Occupational Health Nurse
description:
Job Description:
Occupational Health Nurse
Fort Smith, AR
On-site (min. 4 days a week, 1 day remote with remote location support)
Standard hours with required on-call coverage, plus flexible hours to support shift work on occasion
We are seeking a highly skilled and proactive Occupational Health Nurse (OHN) to support manufacturing sites. This role serves as the clinical expert for occupational health and wellbeing, driving a strong culture of health, safety, and regulatory compliance.
The OHN partners closely with site leadership, HSE, Facilities, HR (P&O), and other stakeholders to influence health outcomes, mitigate risk, and improve workforce wellbeing. This position requires the ability to work independently in a dynamic manufacturing environment while maintaining strong collaboration with site leaders and across a broader Associate Health & Wellbeing network.
The Occupational Health Nurse is the primary clinical authority at the site, responsible for implementing and delivering health and wellbeing programs aligned to organizational strategy. This role supports both a primary (home) site and additional locations, requiring flexibility, adaptability, and a strong partnership mindset.
The OHN plays a critical role in protecting employee health, reducing risk, and enabling business performance through evidence-based occupational health
What are we looking for?
Minimum 3+ years Occupational Health experience
BS in Nursing required, Master’s preferred
Registered Nurse (RN) with an active license within state of residency.   Compact license preferred.
Experience in occupational health, manufacturing, or industrial environments
Strong knowledge of OSHA regulations, workplace safety, and health surveillance programs
Excellent communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills
Current CPR certification
Ability to work independently and autonomously
Project management experience a plus
Previous stakeholder management experience
Strong Business Acumen required
Must have strong collaboration, critical thinking and influencing skills
Workers’ Compensation experience preferred
Ability to travel 25% to sites supported is required
Preferred qualifications
COHN/S (Certified Occupational Health Nurse) preferred
CAOHC Hearing Conservation Certification preferred
Background in ergonomics, injury prevention, case management, and health promotion programs
Previous experience working in a manufacturing site/ in a dynamic fast-paced environment
Experience with population health analytics and data-driven program design
What would be your key responsibilities?
Clinical Care & Case Management
Provide clinical assessment, triage, and management of occupational injuries and illnesses in alignment within the scope of nursing license.
Deliver first aid medical response during clinic hours
Manage return-to-work programs and continuity of care
Manages medical accommodations and the interactive process to ensure ADA compliance.
Maintain accurate, confidential employee health records in compliance with HIPAA and company policy
Regulatory Compliance & Risk Management
Ensure compliance with OSHA, federal and state regulations, and internal policies
Administer and manage required health surveillance programs, including:
Hearing conservation
Respiratory protection
Bloodborne pathogens
Exposure monitoring (chemical, biological, ergonomic risks)
Support incident investigations and partner with HSE to identify and mitigate workplace hazards
Oversee work-related injury/illness case processes and collaborate with claims adjusters and risk management
Health & Wellbeing Strategy
Develop and implement site-specific health action plans based on population health data and risk assessments
Translate health data, dashboards, and insights into actionable recommendations and reporting to site leaders
Evaluate program effectiveness, monitor outcomes, and identify gaps or opportunities
Promote preventative health through education, coaching, and proactive interventions
Business Partnership & Influence
Build trusted, credible partnerships with site leaders and stakeholders to influence a culture of health and safety
Advise leadership on occupational health risks, trends, and regulatory requirements
Engage Associates through walkthroughs, inspections, health promotion events, and training initiatives
Support benefits utilization through health fairs and collaboration with Benefits teams
Ergonomics & Workplace Safety
Conduct and support ergonomic assessments across manufacturing and office environments
Collaborate with HSE to address injury trends and improve workplace design and practices
Collaboration & Continuous Improvement
Partner with the broader Associate Health & Wellbeing team to deploy strategy and share best practices
Participate in communities of practice to exchange insights, tools, and learnings
Stay current with evolving regulations, industry trends, and emerging technologies in Occupational Health
Additional Responsibilities
Regularly engage with Associates across shifts, including off-hours coverage as needed
Operate autonomously while maintaining alignment with enterprise strategy
Support governance, reporting, and continuous improvement efforts
Travel to support additional manufacturing sites

title: Retail Sales Manager - Bentonville (AR)
description:
Job Description:
Job Description:
The Mars Retail Sales Manager is responsible for executing Mars Sales Strategy by applying fact-based selling techniques to influence customer decisions and achieve goals and objectives at Store Level.  Key responsibilities include delivering the Perfect Store, executing Account Headquarter plans, and delivering seasonal sell thru objectives and company priorities by identifying incremental selling opportunities for categories under your responsibility.
The primary role of the Retail Sales Manager (RSM) is to leverage data and insights to sell and execute company strategies and priorities by achieving Sales KPI objectives and creating best in class in-store conditions to engage consumers and drive consumption.  The expectation is that RSM will command strong knowledge of the category, shopper trends and consumer usage occasions, enabling them to effectively sell incremental assortment and in-store solutions.
As an entry point into our MARS Sales organization, RSM is responsible for building strong customer relationships and collaborating across the Sales functions to identify and resolve operational issues.
The position requires a high degree of integrity with the ability to work efficiently and effectively in an independent fashion without direct supervision.  This position is field based within a defined geography and reports directly to a Retail Sales Lead.
Key Responsibilities
Build and maintain long-term, trusted relationships with customers by demonstrating strong consultative selling skills to drive sales, retailer profit, ROI, and market share.
Create value by delivering customized sales presentation(s) based on retailer opportunities and priorities to sell incremental orders and mutually beneficial in-store solutions.
Monitor and analyze performance metrics to identify and execute solutions to achieve territory and region KPIs, retailer category growth, and account/company business targets.
Leverage data and demonstrate a strong priority setting to deliver channel/retailer specific seasonal and limited time offer to sell through targets.
Serve as a primary point of contact for customers, ensuring clear communication of sales priorities, orders, and promotional plans.
Position yourself to be a trusted expert, asking open-ended questions and tailoring solutions to specific needs.
Influence merchandising and operational resources to ensure instore excellence, compliance with execution standards, and timely implementation of sales initiatives.  These include assortment priorities (core and innovation), shelving objectives and planogram integrity, as well as incremental semi-permanent and temporary displays.
Responsible and trusted use of technology is essential, including accurate data entry, analysis of sales data to build a selling story, and effective utilization of company systems to support decision-making and performance tracking.
May have Compression call responsibilities. Comfortable preparing and selling to Market Managers, District Mangers depending on customer base of your territory.
Direct 3rd party providers (where applicable) for in-store execution (including seasonal surge).
Where applicable, sell throughout the year by providing business updates to the store's decision maker and contracts which will support delivery of the distribution, shelving, and display objectives.  Enforce compliance.
Maintain high on shelf availability by working with KDM to address inventory discrepancies and order fulfillment.
Participate in team conference calls, training, and attend all sales meetings.
Responsible for storage facility and managing product rotation, inventory allocation, supplies, etc., in an efficient and effective way.
Job Specifications/Qualifications
This role is an individual contributor.
This role interfaces with customers at store level
This role has a reasonable impact on sales organizations and a reasonable impact on the company.
Education & Professional Qualification:
Bachelor’s Degree
Knowledge/Experience
Minimum Qualifications :
A bachelor’s degree, or HS Diploma and equivalent work experience
Demonstrated proficiency with intermediate technology tools, including mobile devices and basic business applications.
Strong analytical, problem solving, and negotiation skills.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, and relationship building capabilities.
Ability to lift and carry up to 40lbs
Able to sit, stand and/or drive for long periods of time, as well as frequently bend, kneel and stoop
Ability to walk for a minimum of 6 ½ hours per day
Demonstrate ability to work remotely
Subject to outside weather conditions and changing climates
Must live within territory boundaries
Ability to travel overnight if required
Work scheduled may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, and holidays based on business needs.
Role requires daily travel to multiple customer locations and a valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.
Preferred Qualifications:
A bachelor’s degree and significant experience in field sales and territory management
2+ years with at least one year of selling experience
Proven ability to influence customers through professional selling skills and data driven insights.
Experience using technology to analyze performance, manage accounts, and support sales execution.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Work, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Power Bi.
Prior Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) and/or retail sales experience
Prior selling experience in convenience, grocery or Walmart channels.
