title: Senior Director, Strategic Initiatives – Better For You
description:
Job Description:
Who are we?
Accelerator, a global Division of Mars Snacking, is on the front line of unlocking growth across high-potential categories and brands to fuel what’s next for Snacking. It’s home to both emerging and enduring brands, including KIND, TRÜ FRÜ, NATURE’S BAKERY, RXBAR, EGGO, POP-TARTS and RICE KRISPIE TREATS. Combining the scale of Mars with the agility of a start-up, our Division has the ambition to accelerate the future of snacking by delivering products consumers love today, discovering category-shaping innovations for tomorrow and developing entrepreneurial teams whose impact will last for generations.
We’re looking for passionate talent who dare to dream big, agile collaborators who talk straight and decide fast, and driven performers with a growth mindset. We’re proudly part of Mars, while also building something boldly different. If this inspires and energizes you, you’ve found the right place where you can do cool things with fun people for one of the biggest snacking companies in the world!

title: Critical Environment Technician Manager
description:
Overview
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day and we need you as a Data Center Critical Environment Technician Manager.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I CE Technician Manager, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development for all employees and offers trainings and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion trainings and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Prepares and submits highly complex reports as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Root Cause Analysis [RCA] reports) and may review prior reports delivered by less experienced team members. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for highly complex and/or interdependent equipment and disciplines to ensure safe and reliable execution. Reviews completed work using approved tools and procedural templates from less experienced technicians for accuracy and completeness. Provides assignment and completion oversight of team members for mandatory, technical, and procedural training material. Assigns and oversees procedure development and reporting to team members. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Guides, oversees, and performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs for multiple disciplines and multiple equipment types of increasing complexity with no supervision, while serving as a subject matter expert for one discipline - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Provides consultation to colleagues on maintenance and repairs through deep understanding of equipment, systems and their interrelations. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees everyday, complex, large-scale tasks for a single discipline or equipment across disciplines. Ensures follow up action items are addressed in a timely manner. Masters the maintenance of all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance across all disciplines and supports team members with subject matter expertise. Plans, coordinates, and presents maintenance items for review and approval in their area of responsibility.
Provides and/or assigns team members to provide necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site for all procedure levels of risk (LOR). May take part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Engages to address and resolve circumstances when supplier/vendor work has been stopped to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates and/or assigns team members to coordinate across all LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Coordinates with vendor to schedule maintenance and determines availability of equipment/parts, as directed. Resolves or escalates observed vendor quality issues. Reviews and approves vendor supplier field service reports, invoices, and work orders.
Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Leads and provides guidance on coordinating activities and establishing associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities. Advises engineer partners or project management colleagues on project scope process or execution methodology. Presents for review and approval MSOW in their area of responsibility.
Acts as a subject matter expert, performing troubleshooting independently for multiple equipment, systems, subsystems, and component types. Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment in all disciplines work and how to troubleshoot to subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. Ensures troubleshooting completion paths are escalated appropriately and successfully by their team members. Oversees and advises their team members on troubleshooting systems and/or investigates root causes.
Equipment and Systems Operations
Takes part in, and oversees team in the inspection and supervision of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds regularly for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for multiple discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) and understands risks or impacts to other subsystems across the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Ensures all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements. Uses data trends to develop or produce predictive analyses of equipment performance.
Works on complex, advanced tasks (e.g., stabilization, resolution, recovery) independently. Serves as an operations specialist in a major area of operations (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls, generators) and provides oversight and training/mentorship to team members on tasks regarding these subsystems. Demonstrates an understanding of and operates equipment and systems across all disciplines (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Safely and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur, and collects or provides appropriate escalation details or context to support incident management requirements. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides and leads and coordinates emergency monitoring response plans for irregular or malfunctioning conditions. Oversees team during emergency incident management, assigning tasks for corrective repair as appropriate. Communicates directly to leadership, advises the business on the current conditions, safety concerns, and next steps for incident mitigation and/or resolution. Oversees incident detection, analysis, and containment efforts. Serves as technical expert in ensuring emergency operating procedures (EOPs) are consistent with proper incident response.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks utilization and time tracking results for team members, within applicable task management systems. Reviews and validates added required data, documents, changes logged, and procedures upkeep details (related to building management systems and reports) conducted by team members. Guides and coaches team in CMMS usage best practices. Audits and reviews team's data to ensure performance adherence to assigned work tasks. Generates reporting from CMMS for outstanding and ongoing work orders. Generates ad hoc or custom CMMS reports as needed for management. Reviews spare equipment and parts, updates stock, and signal stock replenishment with suppliers and/or coordination with Materials Handling partners.
People Management
Managers deliver success through empowerment and accountability by modeling, coaching, and caring. Model: Live our culture. Embody our values. Practice our leadership principles. Coach: Define team objectives and outcomes. Enable success across boundaries. Help the team adapt and learn. Care: Attract and retain great people. Know each individual’s capabilities and aspirations. Invest in the growth of others.
Other
Embody our culture and values
Qualifications
Required/minimum qualifications
High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.
5+ years mission critical services work/applied learning experience (e.g., high availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.
Background Check Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check:  This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.
Citizenship Verification:  This position requires verification of citizenship due to citizenship-based legal restrictions. Specifically, this position supports United States federal, state, and/or local  government agency customers and is subject to certain citizenship-based restrictions where required or permitted by applicable law. To meet this legal requirement, and as a condition of employment, the successful candidate’s citizenship will be verified with a valid passport.
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.
Preferred qualifications
1+ year(s) experience in a specialized area (e.g., mechanical field, electrical field, controls field) or related field.
Associate's Degree or technical trade certification (e.g., military, trade school), or higher-equivalent education AND 7+ years mission-critical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 10+ years mission critical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.
1+ year(s) people management experience.
Critical Environment Ops M3 - The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is USD $75,400 - $167,900 per year. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $105,800 - $185,300 per year.

We partner with Brand Marketing, Product, Engineering, Data Science, Finance, and Creative to connect marketing investment with customer and business outcomes. Our brand data infrastructure brings together media, audience, creative, and research data so teams can plan, measure, and improve brand investment across markets.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Brand Data Infrastructure Lead to own the data foundations that make brand marketing measurable and scalable. You will define how brand media, campaign, creative, audience, and research data are organized, connected, validated, and made available for decisions. This hands-on role combines brand and media expertise with practical data fluency, turning fragmented platform and partner outputs into dependable datasets and repeatable workflows.

This role sits within Growth Marketing and works closely with Brand Marketing, Media Operations, Growth Platform’s solutions engineering team, Data Engineering, and Data Science. You own Brand’s data roadmap, business definitions, source requirements, data-quality acceptance, and adoption. Engineering partners own production architecture, connector and pipeline implementation, instrumentation, and technical incident resolution. Data Science owns statistical methodology and model development.

Your first priority is to establish consistent campaign and creative taxonomies, dependable media and measurement feeds, clear data-sharing arrangements, and trusted reporting inputs. Build a foundation that supports TV/CTV, online video, social, audio, out-of-home, and other brand channels, with the coverage and history needed for brand tracking, lift studies, incrementally, and marketing mix modeling.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the Brand data infrastructure roadmap. Translate brand strategy, media plans, and measurement needs into prioritized data capabilities, source integrations, quality improvements, and reporting foundations. Balance business value, global coverage, delivery dependencies, cost, and sustained adoption.

 - Define shared data models and taxonomies. Establish consistent campaign, creative, channel, partner, audience, and market definitions, identifiers, reporting grains, and time conventions. Align stakeholders on how datasets connect and how metrics should be interpreted across platforms and markets.

 - Set source and integration requirements. Define the fields, granularity, history, coverage, refresh cadence, and reconciliation needed from platforms, agencies, publishers, and measurement vendors. Partner with engineering on data contracts, integration priorities, acceptance criteria, and ownership throughout the data lifecycle.

 - Enable Brand channels and partner data. Lead data readiness for TV/CTV, video, social, audio, out-of-home, and emerging channels. Ensure new partners and campaigns provide usable delivery, spend, audience, creative, and geographic data, working with Media Operations and channel owners on setup and reporting requirements.

 - Make Brand measurement data ready to use. Coordinate the datasets and metadata required for brand tracking, brand lift, geo experiments, incrementality studies, and marketing mix modeling. Work with Data Science on study requirements and comparability, and connect media and research outputs with relevant product and business outcomes.

 - Own vendor data access and governance readiness. Lead the marketing side of partner evaluation, onboarding, and service reviews. Define required data, delivery terms, permitted uses, and responsibilities with Legal, Privacy, Security, and Procurement, then make those requirements usable for engineering, vendors, and marketing teams.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Integrity team protects people and businesses using ChatGPT, Codex, and the API from fraud, abuse, and harmful misuse. Our work spans payment and promotional abuse, compromised accounts and API credentials, business and advertiser integrity, and emerging misuse of frontier AI capabilities. We also help product teams measure authentic usage so that abuse doesn’t distort decisions about how our products are growing.

Integrity Data Science helps teams decide where to intervene and whether those interventions work. A payment control can prevent fraud while blocking legitimate purchases. A product launch can make it easier for customers to get started while creating new opportunities for abuse. We measure both sides of those decisions.



ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Data Scientist on Integrity, you’ll find emerging abuse patterns, size their impact, and lead the analytical work behind decisions about detection, enforcement, and product launches. You’ll work with Product, Engineering, Research, Policy, and Operations to turn findings into improvements and measure what happens after they ship.

 - Investigate anomalous activity across products. Estimate how common a problem is, who is affected, and what it costs users or the business. Use that evidence to recommend where to focus.

 - Define outcome metrics and guardrails, establish baselines, and build monitoring that surfaces changes in abuse, customer friction, and operational performance.

 - Help build and evaluate detection rules, classifiers, and human review workflows. Use labeled samples and review outcomes to understand what the systems miss, where they flag legitimate activity, and how those errors vary across users and products.

 - Design randomized holdouts and use quasi-experimental or observational methods when randomization is impractical. Estimate harm or fraud losses prevented alongside effects on legitimate users, revenue, compute costs, and review workload. Recommend whether to launch, expand, adjust, or retire a control.

 - Trace where signals, review decisions, or enforcement actions break down. Work with partners to close gaps and build reusable datasets, analyses, and investigation tools.



IDEAL CANDIDATE

 - You use AI tools to investigate large, messy datasets, test hypotheses quickly, and automate recurring analyses. You’re fluent in SQL and Python and can verify AI-generated queries, code, and conclusions against the underlying data.

 - You have strong statistical judgment and experience with experimentation, causal inference, or observational analysis. You can reason from incomplete or biased labels and explain how uncertainty affects a decision.

 - You take ownership of open-ended problems, from deciding what to measure through recommending an action and checking whether it worked.

 - You communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical partners and can explain the tradeoffs behind a recommendation.

 - Experience in integrity, trust and safety, fraud or risk analytics, security analytics, or applied ML evaluation is helpful. Experience evaluating detection systems, human review, or LLM-based classifiers is a plus.

OpenAI’s Robotics team builds hardware and software for general-purpose robots. We work closely with AI researchers and use what we learn from testing on physical robots to guide the next design.

About the Role

We’re hiring an Engineering Manager to lead engineers working on firmware, low-level controls, and systems software for onboard compute. You’ll develop the people doing this work and shape the roadmap with technical leads and partners in hardware and research. You’ll stay close enough to the engineering to help the team make difficult calls, whether that means running one more experiment on the bench or deciding that a change is ready to ship.

In this role, you will:

 - Hire and coach engineers, give them clear feedback, and help them grow. Give experienced engineers room to lead designs and create opportunities for others to take on technical ownership.

 - Set priorities with technical leads and partners in hardware and research. Decide how to staff the work, communicate tradeoffs early, and resolve dependencies that could hold up a hardware milestone.

 - Guide work on embedded systems, from board bring-up and device interfaces to actuator control. Invest in reusable systems software so other engineers can integrate hardware, command it, and understand how it responds.

 - Set the bar for changes that ship to physical robots. Use design reviews, hardware-in-the-loop tests, and measurements of timing, tracking accuracy, and fault recovery to judge readiness.

 - Bring the right people together when a problem crosses disciplines. If an actuator misses its target under load, help the team choose the measurement that will distinguish a controls problem from a firmware or mechanical one.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have managed a team that shipped and supported software on physical hardware. You can point to engineers you hired or coached who went on to lead significant work of their own.

 - Bring depth in firmware, embedded operating systems, or real-time controls, and can reason across all three. Experience integrating custom hardware or off-the-shelf robotic platforms is valuable.

 - Have taken a robotic or electromechanical system from prototype through repeated use. You know when a quick bench test will answer a design question and when reliability needs to be demonstrated under load.

 - Have led work across teams with different priorities. You can make a clear decision as requirements change, explain it to partners, and give engineers the context and autonomy to carry it through.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence (AGI) which benefits all of humanity. This long-term undertaking brings the world’s best scientists, engineers, and business professionals into one lab together to accomplish this.

The GTM Agentic Workflows team is building OpenAI’s agentic go-to-market operating system. We work with sellers, GTM leaders, and partners in GTM Systems, Data Science, and Product to connect customer intelligence to account strategy, helping teams prioritize opportunities, grow adoption across accounts, and spend time where it matters most.

About the Role

As an individual contributor on the GTM Agentic Workflows team, you’ll own the design, rollout, and performance of processes and workflows across the customer lifecycle, from lead routing through deal execution, delivery, and consumption. Orchestration is central to this role. You’ll bring sellers, GTM leaders, and cross-functional partners together around a shared outcome, then connect the work of people, systems, and agentic workflows to deliver it.

In this role, you will:

 - Prioritize problems with GTM leaders and the field. Look at where sellers repeat work, where deals stall, and which handoffs break down. Use the frequency and impact of those problems to decide what to tackle first.

 - Strengthen the foundations of GTM workflows. Set the strategy for enriching person and company data, and partner with GTM Systems on lead routing and how sellers manage accounts and opportunities in Salesforce.

 - Orchestrate delivery across teams. Align owners on the outcome, sequence work across functions, and resolve competing priorities. Make clear who decides, what information carries forward, and when the next team can act.

 - Design and launch workflows with Product and Enterprise Systems. Define what triggers the workflow, what information an agent needs, and when a person should review or approve an action. Pilot with field teams and partner with Enablement on rollout.

 - Own performance after launch. Measure adoption alongside outcomes such as lead response time, accuracy of proposed updates, and time to complete a handoff. Use those results and field feedback to decide what to improve next.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 8+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, or related roles at a high-growth technology company

 - Strong systems thinking with deep experience designing and scaling sales systems, processes, and workflows across the full sales lifecycle

 - Experience taking a multi-step GTM workflow from a field problem through rollout. You can explain what you automated, where people retained judgment, and how you measured whether it worked.

 - Strong proficiency in Salesforce and data tools (e.g., SQL, Excel). Strong analytical skills with high attention to detail

 - Experience with territory design, account structures, and pipeline management

 - A track record of leading through influence. You can point to a cross-functional initiative where you brought teams with competing priorities to a decision and saw it through to delivery.

With that aim in mind, we are responsible for developing and executing strategies that drive awareness, engagement, and usage for OpenAI’s products and platform amongst our core audiences. We then partner closely with Product, Engineering, Research, Comms, and Design teams to create a cohesive customer experience across all our channels. Our focus extends beyond just promoting product features; we aim to provide valuable insights and resources that help our users make the most out of AI technologies.

We are seeking an Integrated Marketing Manager that can lead the development and execution of multi-channel marketing campaigns that drive awareness, engagement, and conversion across our key audiences. This role is perfect for a creative thinker and skilled collaborator who thrives bringing together different teams for a common goal in an ever-changing environment.

 - from brief and conceptual development to stakeholder alignment, flawless execution, launch and post-campaign analysis

 - Traditional + Digital Marketing Expertise: Proficiency across channels, including TV, OOH, social, content, performance marketing, and events.

title: Lauch Producer, Business Marketing
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Business Marketing helps knowledge workers, developers, and business decision-makers understand and adopt OpenAI’s products, supporting both self-serve growth and our managed sales team. Our creative work makes complex capabilities clear, grounded, and human as they move from the lab into businesses and everyday work.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a hands-on Launch Producer to build and run a repeatable, scalable creative production engine for Business Marketing launches, spanning new models, products, and capabilities, as well as solutions and use cases.

You’ll help shape the right creative and video approach for each launch, then lead production from brief through delivery. Most launches center on owned and social channels, and leverage video as a primary medium to explain new products and capabilities. Our largest launches also shape broader brand marketing, requiring coordination with Integrated Marketing and Media.

This role combines building the system with running the work. You should be equally comfortable improving a workflow, leading a shoot, and partnering with a motion designer.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Lead launch intake and planning, aligning creative scope, resources, and timelines with launch priorities.

 - Partner with Product Marketing, Integrated Marketing, creative leads, and subject-matter experts to translate launch goals, audiences, messaging, and technical capabilities into compelling briefs, scripts, demos, and customer stories.

 - Produce videos at varying levels of fidelity, including demos, motion graphics, sizzle videos, explainers, and talking-head or testimonial videos featuring OpenAI talent and customers.

 - Lead production end to end: budgets, schedules, resourcing, shoots, post-production, and delivery. Consolidate feedback and approvals, manage dependencies, and surface risks and decisions early so assets are ready to ship.

 - Partner with Creative Operations to assemble and manage the right production team for each launch, drawing on your trusted bench of freelancers, agencies, and production partners alongside internal talent. Set clear scopes, expectations, and quality standards.

 - Plan assets for owned and social distribution, including formats, cutdowns, and channel-specific adaptations. Coordinate usage rights, accessibility, quality control, and final delivery requirements with the relevant partners.

 - Partner with Demand teams to translate launch strategy into demand-generation creative, informing briefs, asset needs, and cutdowns while those teams own demand execution.

 - Coordinate with Integrated Marketing and Media on major launches with broader brand and paid-media implications.

 - Build reusable workflows, templates, and production approaches. Use AI-enabled tools, post-launch learnings, and asset performance to improve speed, quality, and effectiveness without adding unnecessary process.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE

 - Experience: 12+ years in integrated creative production, digital production, program management, or a related field, with a proven track record of managing complex creative initiatives.

 - A true operator’s mindset: you can build a reliable production system and keep multiple launches moving through it.

 - Strong storytelling and creative judgment, with hands-on experience leading video shoots and working with motion designers, editors, and other production specialists.

 - An established network of creative and production talent, and sound judgment about the right team, scope, and approach for each brief, budget, and timeline.

 - Fluency in post-production and delivering assets across social, owned, and demand channels.

 - Clear, proactive communication and a collaborative working style. You build trust across disciplines, make tradeoffs visible, and keep teams aligned through shifting priorities.

 - A scrappy, resourceful approach and comfort with ambiguity and tight timelines. You know when a simple demo is enough and when a launch needs a more ambitious treatment.

 - A portfolio demonstrating end-to-end production leadership across fast-turn and larger-scale work, with your specific contribution and outcomes clearly identified.

title: Manager, Data Engineering, Trust & Safety
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Applied organization brings OpenAI’s most advanced technology to people and organizations around the world through products such as ChatGPT and the APIs that power a growing ecosystem of developer and enterprise applications. Data Engineering builds and operates trustworthy, secure, and reliable data systems that support decisions across OpenAI.



The Trust & Safety Data Engineering team builds privacy-safe foundations that help OpenAI understand and mitigate abuse, launch products safely, and operate accountable safety systems at scale.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Data Engineering Manager to lead the Trust & Safety Data Engineering team. This role is accountable for the team’s health, talent, priorities, and results, as well as the data strategy for abuse detection, investigations, enforcement, safety measurement, launch readiness, and transparency reporting.



You will partner with senior individual contributors and cross-functional leaders to turn sensitive, fast-moving safety needs into durable, governed data products and ML data capabilities.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build and grow a high-performing, inclusive team; hire well, develop senior engineers, give clear feedback, and manage performance effectively.

 - Define the data strategy and roadmap with senior technical leaders, establishing clear ownership and delegation boundaries so decisions are made at the right level.

 - Lead the delivery of scalable, governed datasets, pipelines, and data products for critical Trust & Safety workflows.

 - Enable ML development with high-quality features, labels, training data, evaluation datasets, and production data pipelines.

 - Set strong standards for metric definitions, data quality, privacy, security, access controls, documentation, reliability, observability, and incident response.

 - Partner across Trust & Safety, Integrity, Investigations, Engineering, Data Science, Policy, Privacy, and Operations to translate ambiguous needs into measurable outcomes.

 - Set clear goals, make explicit capacity and priority tradeoffs, and communicate progress, risks, and commitments across technical and operational stakeholders.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have led and scaled data engineering teams, with evidence of strong hiring, senior-talent development, performance management, and sustained delivery through the team.

 - Bring strong technical judgment across large-scale data systems—including SQL, Python or Scala, Spark, orchestration, data modeling, streaming, and lakehouse or warehouse architectures—and can challenge designs and guide senior engineers without owning every implementation detail.

 - Have experience in trust and safety, integrity, abuse prevention, fraud, investigations, risk, privacy, or another domain where data systems inform consequential decisions.

 - Build strong cross-functional partnerships and turn ambiguous needs into clear ownership, durable data contracts, technical roadmaps, and reliable execution.

 - Care deeply about privacy, security, governance, data quality, and the operational health of systems used for sensitive workflows.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Trust & Safety teams across OpenAI move faster because they can rely on trustworthy, well-owned data foundations provided by this team.

We are seeking a senior leader to build, manage, and scale a high-performing team of Delivery Leads responsible for orchestrating complex, high-impact AI initiatives from scoping and planning through launch, adoption, and measurable customer value.



The Delivery Leads team serves as the central orchestration layer across OpenAI’s most strategic customer engagements, bringing together account teams, technical specialists, Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), customers, and delivery partners around integrated delivery plans, clear commitments, and shared outcomes. The team drives execution across multiple workstreams, resolves critical dependencies, and ensures successful deployments translate into sustained adoption, consumption, and business impact.



In this role, you will own the team's strategy, operating model, and delivery excellence while hiring, developing, and leading senior customer-facing talent. You will stay close to our most complex customer engagements, providing executive-level guidance, navigating delivery risks, and building the scalable mechanisms, playbooks, and operating rhythms that enable consistent execution as our business grows.



This role is based in New York or San Francisco and follows a hybrid schedule of three days per week in office. Regional travel is expected.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Own the strategy and operating model for Delivery Leads, defining how the team engages across OpenAI's most strategic accounts, establishes delivery accountability, and drives consistent execution from pre-sales scoping through launch and initial adoption.

 - Hire, lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of Delivery Leads, building a team with strong technical fluency, executive presence, commercial judgment, and the ability to lead complex enterprise AI transformation programs.

 - Oversee delivery execution across a portfolio of strategic customers, ensuring priority AI initiatives have integrated delivery plans, clear milestones, accountable owners, dependencies, resource commitments, and measurable success criteria.

 - Partner cross-functionally with Sales, Technical Success teams, FDE, Product, and external delivery partners to ensure seamless coordination, clear ownership, and an integrated customer delivery experience.

 - Shape the evolution of OpenAI's delivery model, translating field insights into improvements in customer engagement, delivery methodologies, resourcing strategies, product capabilities, and organizational effectiveness.




YOU'LL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - 8+ years of experience leading complex enterprise technology delivery or transformation programs, including 4+ years managing technical delivery, professional services, customer engineering, or enterprise transformation teams.

 - Proven track record building and scaling high-performing teams in fast-growing technology environments, with demonstrated success developing senior talent and establishing scalable operating models.

 - Deep experience overseeing complex, multi-workstream enterprise deployments, including programs spanning technical implementation, systems integration, organizational change, and multiple internal and external stakeholders.

title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer, Data Center Modular Builds
description:
About the Team

OpenAI and its capital and technology partners are building a global network of data centers for demanding AI workloads. The Infrastructure Quality team sets and verifies quality, reliability, and performance requirements for equipment across that network.

We work with manufacturing partners, general contractors, engineers, and operations staff from supplier qualification through commissioning. Together, we verify that equipment arrives ready for installation, startup, and long-term service.

About the Role

As a Manufacturing Quality Engineer for Data Center Modular Builds, you will own supplier manufacturing and integration quality for modular systems, including hot aisle containment (HAC), modular cooling units (MCUs), and electrical skids. Working with mechanical and electrical integrators and their suppliers, you will lead supplier qualification, support product and process development, and translate engineering requirements into manufacturing controls, inspections, and acceptance criteria.

You will partner with cross-functional teams to monitor production and integration quality, conduct audits, and resolve risks to integrated products acceptance and delivery. You will also serve as the primary quality contact for site escalations involving manufacturing or integration defects in modular systems and(OFCI) components. Through structured root-cause investigations, corrective action, and closed-loop learning (CLL), you will drive resolution and feed field lessons back into supplier processes to prevent recurrence and improve future builds.

Key responsibilities

Modular Systems Quality and Supplier Development

 - Lead supplier qualification and support product and process development for mechanical and electrical integrators.

 - Oversee manufacturing and integration quality for modular builds, including HACs, MCUs, and electrical skids.

 - Work with integrators and suppliers to translate engineering requirements and critical-to-quality (CTQ) characteristics into practical manufacturing controls, inspection points, and acceptance criteria.

 - Develop and drive supplier improvement plans (SIPs) using the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) approach to strengthen manufacturing and integration processes.

 - Use production data, audit findings, test results, and supplier scorecards to identify systemic or recurring issues, prioritize improvements, and measure sustained results.

Site Escalations and Corrective Action

 - Serve as the primary quality point of contact for escalated site issues attributable to manufacturing and integration failures, coordinating containment and resolution with site teams and supplier factories.

 - Lead root-cause and corrective-action (RCCA) investigations using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys. Verify root causes, track corrective and preventive actions to closure, and confirm their effectiveness.

 - Apply closed-loop learning (CLL) to incorporate field findings and lessons learned into supplier and integrator manufacturing controls and future builds, preventing recurrence.

Manufacturing and Integration Monitoring

 - Partner with Quality Program and Manufacturing Operations teams to monitor production and integration progress, quality controls, inspection results, and factory test readiness. Identify emerging risks and coordinate timely action with suppliers.

 - Conduct product and process audits during and after manufacturing and integration to verify compliance with engineering requirements, approved procedures, and quality standards. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.

 - Align production checkpoints, inspections, and factory testing requirements with suppliers, engineering, sourcing, supply chain, commissioning, and quality teams. Coordinate deviation resolution and escalate risks to equipment acceptance or delivery.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, or industrial engineering.

 - At least 10 years of data center industry experience spanning quality engineering and manufacturing engineering.

 - Experience working with integrators and suppliers across multiple tiers to manage quality throughout the product lifecycle, from OFCI component manufacturing through integration and site issue resolution, and drive product and process improvements.

 - Ability to define CTQs and acceptance criteria, develop inspection and test checklists, review test results, and maintain auditable quality records.

 - Experience monitoring supplier production, conducting product and process audits, managing controlled documents and deviations, and using supplier scorecards to drive improvement.

 - Demonstrated experience leading root-cause investigations and corrective actions for manufacturing or field issues using structured methods such as 8D and 5 Whys, and driving continuous improvement through PDCA.

 - Ability to coordinate supplier schedules and plan inspections and tests across multiple equipment programs.

 - Ability to communicate quality requirements, resolve issues, and coordinate decisions across suppliers, engineering, commissioning, sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, operations, and construction teams.

 - Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40% of the time to supplier manufacturing facilities and data center project sites.

Preferred Skills

 - Technical knowledge of data center infrastructure, including mechanical, electrical, and controls systems.

 - Experience in supplier performance management for mission-critical facilities.

 - ASQ Certified Quality Engineer, Quality Manager, or Quality Auditor.

 - Experience in industrial or high-volume manufacturing environments.

title: Mechanical Design Engineer, Battery Pack
description:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. As a Mechanical Design Engineer on the Robotics team, you’ll design battery packs for robots and help define how those packs integrate into the rest of the system. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you’ll own mechanical designs from early architecture and packaging through prototyping, validation, and production. title: Model Policy Manager, Emerging AI Misuse
description:
About the Team

The Model Policy team within OpenAI’s Safety Systems organization defines how increasingly capable AI models should behave in real-world settings. We turn research on emerging risks into model behavior policies, evaluations, and safeguards.

About the Role

As AI systems become more capable, the same advances that expand their legitimate uses can also lower barriers to harm. Emerging misuse risks range from AI assistance with conventional weapons development and the misuse of AI-enabled robotics to fraud, impersonation, and other forms of abuse that people can carry out at scale using AI agents. You’ll build threat models for how people could misuse AI in digital and physical settings, assess what access to AI changes in practice, and use that evidence to define how models should respond.

This role is based in San Francisco. We offer relocation support and work from the office three days a week, with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays.

In this role, you will: 

 - Build and update threat models as capabilities evolve. Assess what people could plausibly do, what expertise and resources they would need, and how AI changes those barriers.

 - Define when models should help, limit assistance, or refuse in situations where the same capability has legitimate and harmful uses.

 - Turn expert safety judgment into instructions, training examples, and evaluations that teach models when to help, when to limit assistance, and when to refuse.

 - Turn threat models into evaluation scenarios and grading guidance. Analyze model outputs, red-team findings, and deployment data to identify where models enable misuse or block legitimate work.

 - Partner with research, engineering, security, and product teams to apply findings to model training, deployment decisions, and monitoring.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

 - Have hands-on experience building, testing, or assessing dual-use technologies, or a track record of threat modeling grounded in how people use and misuse real systems.

 - Demonstrate deep practical experience in one relevant domain and the judgment to know when to bring in experts from others.

 - Are able to assess whether a capability demonstrated in a test materially changes what someone could do outside it.

 - Can translate technical evidence and uncertainty into clear policy boundaries and measurable evaluation criteria.

 - Have experience analyzing gold sets, evaluation results, and training data to spot inconsistent human labels, assess how annotator disagreement affects measured performance, and decide what to investigate next.

 - Are comfortable working hands-on with model data and evaluation results, including inspecting examples, analyzing failure patterns, assessing data quality, and distinguishing policy failures from grader, model, or system failures.

 - Use empirical evidence to develop and refine safety policies and safeguards.

 - Work well across disciplines and revises their judgment as capabilities and evidence change.

 - Enjoy fast-paced, collaborative research environments where priorities shift as models, evidence, and risks change.

title: Product Manager, Native Learning and Credentials
description:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

We are exploring how learning, practice, assessment, and evidence of capability can become part of the product experience for people using ChatGPT, Codex, and other OpenAI products at work. Our work focuses on helping people build useful AI skills in the flow of work while giving organizations a clearer view of progress, capability, and readiness.

About the Role

As Product Lead, Native Learning & Credentials, you will define and drive a new product area at the intersection of AI, enterprise learning, assessment, and safe and beneficial use.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who is at their best close to the work. You will take a broad customer and business opportunity and make it concrete: identify the first problem worth solving, define the learner and enterprise journeys, sequence an initial product, and lead the work through engineering alignment, launch, measurement, and iteration. You will work with a small, cross-functional group.

We’re looking for people who combine product depth with GM-level ownership. You should be comfortable moving between customer needs, product strategy, technical architecture, operating design, evidence standards, and business outcomes. You will partner closely with engineering, design, program, learning, and assessment experts, bringing the judgment to make sound tradeoffs while respecting their domain expertise.

The area is early, and the path is not predetermined. Success will come from simplifying ambiguity, shipping focused product proofs, and using evidence to guide investment. If the area earns sustained investment, this role can grow into broader leadership of the product and program over time.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Define the customer, learner, and business problem for Native Learning and Credentials, starting with enterprise adoption and workforce capability.

 - Own the product strategy and roadmap across learning, applied practice, assessment, credential decisions and issuance, learner state, and enterprise reporting.

 - Personally own the product brief, user journeys, requirements, PRDs, roadmap, milestones, non-goals, and decision records that turn an ambiguous opportunity into an executable plan.

 - Partner deeply with engineering and design to define the experience and technical foundations, make architecture and sequencing tradeoffs, and deliver high-quality products.

 - Decide which capabilities OpenAI should build, buy, or access through partners, balancing speed, differentiation, trust, quality, and operational simplicity.

 - Work with learning, assessment, legal, safety, privacy, security, and accessibility partners to establish credible evidence standards and a trustworthy learner experience. Ensure that credential claims are supported by reliable evidence of capability.

 - Establish instrumentation and evaluation across product quality, learner progress, application to real work, adoption, and enterprise value. Use these measures to guide iteration and investment.

 - Create a coherent experience across OpenAI product surfaces and relevant learning, credential, and partner systems, with clear system boundaries and ownership.

 - Remain accountable beyond launch, working with data, support, and operations partners to improve the product, refine the business model, and develop a resource plan grounded in evidence.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have significant product leadership experience in technically complex, user-facing products, including leading a 0-to-1 product from an unclear opportunity through engineering execution, launch, measurement, and meaningful adoption.

 - Have strong technical product judgment across user experience, architecture, services and APIs, identity and state, data, telemetry, evaluation, reliability, and operational readiness.

 - Have personally written or directly owned high-quality product requirements, roadmaps, and technical decision documents.

 - Earn engineers’ trust by defining problems clearly, making sound scope choices, exposing uncertainty, and following through.

 - Have experience building for enterprise or professional users, including the needs of organizational buyers and administrators across reporting, support, security, integrations, and deployment.

 - Communicate clearly across executive, customer, design, engineering, and operational audiences, and lead across organizational boundaries without relying on formal authority.

 - Work effectively with a small team, creating clarity through focused scope, reusable foundations, and an explicit decision cadence.

 - Exercise sound judgment with incomplete information and constrained resources, distinguishing reversible experiments from consequential commitments.

 - Care deeply about the integrity of products that measure or represent human capability and work effectively with learning, assessment, credentialing, and trust experts.

 - Want to build the foundations of a product area and have the range to take on broader program or team leadership as it grows.

Additional experience that would be helpful includes:

 - Building learning, assessment, credentialing, coaching, onboarding, behavior change, developer education, or workforce development products.

 - Building AI or LLM products, agent-assisted workflows, model evaluations, or personalized experiences.

 - Working with identity verification, credential issuance, learning records, skills systems, enterprise integrations, or assessment integrity.

In support of that mission, the SMB Marketing team helps small and medium-sized businesses understand and adopt ChatGPT Business and OpenAI’s B2B solutions. We build a deep understanding of business owners and teams, shape relevant product narratives, and drive awareness, adoption, and growth.

We take a data-driven approach to understand SMB audiences, uncover customer needs, and translate AI capabilities into practical business value. We partner closely with Growth, Product Marketing, Sales, Partnerships, Product, Research, Communications, and Design to deliver a cohesive customer experience across discovery, evaluation, purchase, adoption, and expansion.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Product Marketing Manager, SMB to bring together SMB insights, market understanding, and product knowledge to shape positioning, inform product priorities, and deliver go-to-market initiatives that drive adoption and measurable business impact.

You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, Growth, and Partnerships to understand SMB needs, translate complex AI capabilities into clear customer value, and bring new products and features to market. This role is ideal for someone who combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, independently navigates ambiguity, and brings cross-functional partners together to deliver results.

In this role, you will:

 - Define the product and marketing strategy for a component of OpenAI’s SMB portfolio in partnership with cross-functional partners

 - Own positioning and messaging for your product area, translating complex capabilities into compelling narratives for different SMB owners and teams across relevant industries and business functions. 

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to bring customer needs and market insights into roadmap discussions and product decisions.

 - Develop and drive go-to-market plans for new products and partner integrations, owning marketing execution from planning through launch and ongoing adoption.

title: Protection Scientist Engineer, Integrity
description:
About the Team

The Integrity team is responsible for the scaled systems that help identify and respond to bad actors and harm on OpenAI’s platforms. We protect users and the wider world by developing responses to complex harms and building the harm protections needed for new product and model launches. Integrity’s work spans not only across frontier harms like biological weapons and cybersecurity, but also high severity abuses such as child safety, nation-state misuse, and violence.

About the Role

Protection Scientists within Integrity design, orchestrate, and mature systems of defence against usage harms enabled by OpenAI's products. We are systems thinkers that combine deep harm domain expertise with breadth across investigation, data science, machine learning, policy and operations. Our distinctive strength is understanding how these disciplines fit together and translating between them to design and build effective systems of defence.

In San Francisco, we are hiring for protection work focused on sextortion, trafficking, national security (including nation-state misuse), and jailbreaks. Depending on your domain expertise, your work could include identifying AI-enabled coercion and exploitation, detecting misuse that supports trafficking, uncovering coordinated activity by state-linked actors, or investigating attempts to circumvent model safeguards. You will translate these evolving threats into detection systems and interventions that reduce harm.

Your core hands-on technical responsibility is harm detection. You will design, build, evaluate and maintain production detection systems, drawing on investigative expertise, data and shared engineering platforms. You will develop signals and classifiers that identify abusive behaviour and patterns across accounts and activity, and adapt them as adversaries change tactics.

You will also own the strategy and cross-functional delivery of protection work for a harm area or product launch. Working closely with investigators and other domain experts, you will ground the design in a deep understanding of how the harm occurs and translate that understanding into a system of defence. You will connect detection with policy, review, interventions, enforcement and measurement, continually calibrating the system against real cases and expert judgement as it scales.

You will identify what needs to be built or changed and make it happen. Success requires setting clear priorities, aligning partners, resolving dependencies and communicating evidence, decisions and trade-offs crisply. It also requires a willingness to jump in and work directly on whatever is blocking system effectiveness, using your breadth of skills.

This role is based in our San Francisco office and includes participation in an on-call rotation that may involve resolving urgent escalations outside normal working hours. Some investigations may involve sensitive content, including sexual, violent or otherwise disturbing material.

In this role, you will:

 - Define and drive protection strategy for a harm area or launch. Translate ambiguous risks into goals, priorities and roadmaps, and make trade-offs based on evidence, risk and available capacity.

 - Directly build and maintain harm detection. Develop production signals, classifiers and pipelines using SQL, Python, machine learning and language models, integrating with shared engineering platforms.

 - Lead cross-functional execution. Translate between specialist roles, establish shared understanding and ownership, resolve technical and organisational dependencies, and communicate recommendations and specific asks clearly.

 - Investigate exploitation and national security threats within your area of focus. Work with domain experts to understand actor behaviour, recognise patterns of coercion, exploitation or coordinated misuse, and turn case findings into detection criteria.

 - Connect detection to effective action. Partner with Policy and Operations to develop review and escalation protocols, distinguish abusive activity from legitimate use, and improve interventions as new cases reveal gaps.

 - Evaluate and improve the complete system of defence. Measure remaining harm, detection quality and intervention effectiveness and collaborate with Data Science on more sophisticated metrics. Use expert feedback and operational outcomes to guide improvements.

 - Protect product and model launches. Define data, detection and review requirements; establish monitoring; investigate gaps and critical escalations; and drive improvements informed by post-launch findings.

 - Scale effective approaches with language models, agents and reusable tools. Choose where automation and human judgement are needed, and build documentation and processes that improve reliability and help others extend the work.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Think in systems. You have enough breadth across technical, analytical, investigative and operational disciplines to understand how they fit together, recognise gaps and translate between specialist perspectives.

 - Bring deep expertise in at least one of sextortion, trafficking, national security, jailbreaks or a closely related harm domain. Relevant backgrounds may include trust and safety investigations, counter-exploitation, threat intelligence, investigations of state-linked actors, or adversarial testing of AI safeguards. You do not need expertise across all of these areas.

 - Have experience investigating adversarial behaviour and translating incomplete, evolving evidence into actionable signals. You can connect individual cases to broader patterns while being explicit about uncertainty and the risk of misidentifying legitimate activity.

 - Are proficient in SQL and Python and have experience writing reliable and efficient production code for detection and data processing. Additional ML or SWE experience is a plus.

 - Can apply quantitative analysis and machine-learning methods to measure risks and evaluate system effectiveness. You understand the limitations of your data and can reason about missed harms, false positives and appropriate interventions. Additional DS/measurement background is a plus.

 - Have experience setting strategy and delivering complex, cross-functional technical projects. You can turn an ambiguous problem into a plan, align people with different priorities and drive work through to completion.

 - Communicate clearly and concisely in writing and conversation. You can explain technical findings, make actionable recommendations and surface uncertainty and trade-offs to different audiences.

 - Can use language models and other automation to scale analytical, investigative or operational work, with evaluation and human oversight appropriate to the problem.

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Health
description:
About the Team

The Health team, within OpenAI’s broader Post Training organization, has a mission to ensure AGI improves health for all humanity.

Improving human health will be one of the defining impacts of AGI. Hundreds of millions of people already turn to ChatGPT for questions about their health and millions of clinicians use it weekly to support care delivery. Increasingly capable models create an opportunity to make high-quality medical intelligence more accessible across patients and clinicians—raising the floor of human health—and accelerate the new capabilities and scientific advances that raise the ceiling of human health.

Our job is to make those benefits real. We work across the full model stack—pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, post-training, evaluations, harnessing, and deployment—and connect that research to the patients, clinicians, and real-world outcomes we aim to improve.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher who wants to build frontier health capabilities and turn them into impact at scale. This is a role for someone who can take an important, underdefined problem from 0→1: identify the right bet, build what’s needed to test it, and drive it all the way to a measurable improvement in the models and products we actually ship.

We’re especially excited about two kinds of people: researchers with the technical depth to move the frontier in pretraining, reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, or evals; and researchers with real depth in developing frontier biomedical AI capabilities. Prior experience in healthcare is helpful but not required. Research excellence, velocity, ownership, and alignment with the mission are most important to us.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own a high-leverage research direction end to end—from deciding which problem matters and how to measure it, to designing and running experiments, to integrating successful work into frontier models.

 - Develop scalable methods across pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, and post-training to improve health reasoning, knowledge, reliability, calibration, and behavior.

 - Build and study RL environments grounded in real health problems; understand which data and training setups produce robust, generalizable improvements rather than just higher benchmark scores.

 - Create meaningful, trustworthy, and unsaturated evaluations that tell us whether our models are actually getting better at what matters for patients and clinicians.

 - Advance new 0→1 capabilities in health that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute.

 - Develop models and agents that can work over longitudinal, multimodal health data to produce useful predictions, surface new scientific insights, and support better individual- and population-level decisions.

 - Work closely with researchers, engineers, clinicians, and product teams to bring health capabilities into the models and products used by hundreds of millions of people.

 - Help establish that AI improves real health outcomes, not just that it can produce impressive answers or demos.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Care deeply about using increasingly capable AI to improve human health, and take seriously the responsibility of deploying it safely.

 - Have an unusually strong track record in machine learning or AI research, with the depth to push at least one important area forward: pretraining, reinforcement learning / post-training, evals (not necessarily specific to health); or substantial depth in a relevant frontier health / biomedical AI problem.

 - Are a hands-on builder: you can design experiments, write and debug code, work directly with data and training infrastructure, and move quickly from an idea to evidence.

 - Have strong research taste and can distinguish an important problem or a promising approach from an interesting one.

 - Own ambiguous problems end to end, and are willing to learn whatever is missing to get the job done.

 - Stay goal-oriented rather than method-oriented, and don’t shy away from unglamorous work if it is the highest-leverage path to impact.

 - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype.

 - Enjoy working with low-ego, ambitious people across research, engineering, medicine, and product.

 - Bonus: Experience with health AI, longitudinal health data, or clinical research.

 

If you want your work to help make medical intelligence widely accessible—and to work on some of the most important frontier problems at the intersection of AI, science, and human health—we’d love to hear from you.

About the Team

The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization.

Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT.

Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations.

About the Role

We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship.

We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required.

In this role, you will

 - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals.

 - Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models.

 - Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings.

 - Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss.

 - Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements.

 - Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users.

You might thrive in this role if you

 - Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models.

 - Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit.

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Post-Training — Collective Alignment (User Signals)
description:
About the Team

The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT.

Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. Our team develops scientific approaches to understanding these signals and translating them into improvements in model behavior through evaluations, reward modeling, and post-training.

About the Role

As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time.

You will develop new approaches to extracting meaningful learning signals from complex user interactions and incorporating those signals into model training.

This role requires strong deep learning research skills, scientific rigor, and curiosity about how people interact with AI. You will design controlled experiments and ablations, critically examine the relationship between offline evaluations and online model behavior, and work closely with research, product, and data science teams to understand whether improvements translate into meaningful value for users.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop novel methods for learning from human feedback and user interaction signals.

 - Research approaches to incorporating feedback into reward modeling, reinforcement learning, and post-training.

 - Design rigorous experiments and ablation studies to isolate the effects of new data, objectives, and training methods.

 - Develop offline evaluations and investigate their relationship with online experiments and real-world user outcomes.

 - Analyze unexpected results, investigate discrepancies between evaluation metrics and user behavior, and develop hypotheses to guide further research.

 - Evaluate tradeoffs and regressions to improve targeted model behaviors while preserving broader capabilities.

 - Collaborate with research, alignment, product, and data science teams.

 - Implement and debug experiments across large-scale deep learning research systems.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a strong background in deep learning research through academic or industry experience.

 - Have demonstrated research ability through publications or substantive research contributions in deep learning or LLM post-training.

 - Have experience developing new machine learning methods and evaluating them through rigorous, hypothesis-driven experimentation.

 - Think critically about experimental design, measurement, and what evaluation results do and do not establish about model behavior.

 - Are comfortable designing ablations, investigating surprising results, and reasoning about the relationship between offline metrics and real-world outcomes.

 - Have strong programming skills and experience working with complex ML codebases.

 - Are curious about how people interact with AI and how those interactions can inform better models.

Nice to have:

 - Experience with RLHF, reinforcement learning, or modern LLM post-training.

 - Research or demonstrated interest in AI alignment, human feedback, or user signals.

 - Experience with online experimentation, evaluation methodology, or learning from noisy and biased feedback.

 - Experience connecting machine learning research with real-world product behavior.
