title: Researcher, Cyber Safety Training
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world. The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback.

Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces. We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll work directly on the large training runs that shape OpenAI’s frontier models. Your focus will be teaching models to help people do legitimate security work while recognizing when their assistance could enable harm. A model that refuses to help a defender investigate a security issue can fail in a different way from one that helps someone misuse it. You’ll study both kinds of mistakes and use what you learn to improve the next training run.

We’re looking for someone with hands-on machine learning experience who wants to bring security judgment into model training. You might come from cybersecurity and want to go deeper on post-training, or from reinforcement learning and want to build substantial expertise in cybersecurity.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Work with cybersecurity researchers to identify situations where context changes what help a model should give.

 - Design complex and realistic cyber safety evaluations.

 - Research post-training techniques that robustly improves the cyber safety of the frontier models.

 - Work with the core post-training team to bring promising methods into large model runs and verify that the safety improvements hold at scale.

 - Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including T&S, legal, policy and other research teams, to ensure that our products meet the highest safety standards.
   
   


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have trained or fine-tuned models yourself and can describe an experiment where you used the results to change how you trained the next model.

 - Bring practical security judgment from industry work, a research project, collaboration with a security team, or capture-the-flag competitions. We also welcome reinforcement learning practitioners motivated to develop that judgment alongside security researchers.

 - Can build and debug the code behind a training experiment, from preparing data to checking whether a change in the results reflects a real change in model behavior.

 - Enjoy working through ambiguous cases with domain experts and translating what you learn into concrete decisions about how a model should respond.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI Consumer Devices is building the next generation of products that bring powerful AI into people’s everyday lives. Guided by OpenAI’s mission to ensure AGI benefits all of humanity, our team combines world-class researchers, engineers, designers, and operators who care deeply about creating useful, intuitive, and responsible technology. You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside exceptional people on ambitious, zero-to-one challenges at the intersection of hardware, software, and AI. This is a chance to help define an entirely new category of products—and shape how people experience AI in the future.

The Operating Systems team is critical in this mission, turning sophisticated hardware and AI capabilities into a reliable, trusted platform. Security is central to that work: we define trust boundaries, integrate hardware-backed protections, isolate sensitive context, and establish the guardrails that let AI applications and agents act safely, privately, and under user control.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Software Security Architect to define the security architecture for OpenAI’s next-generation operating system. You’ll work alongside hardware security architects and partner with operating system, silicon, firmware, privacy, and product teams to protect users, their devices, and their data.

This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who can connect operating system internals, hardware-backed security, and real-world product constraints. Your work will shape the platform’s trust model, protect sensitive information, and set the technical foundations for AI that is safe, private, and under user control.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Define the operating system’s security architecture, trust boundaries, privilege model, and protections for sensitive user data.

 - Partner with hardware security architects to integrate roots of trust, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and processor security capabilities into the operating system.

 - Design foundational platform defenses, including secure boot, code signing, attestation, secure updates, key protection, and device recovery.

 - Establish isolation and access controls across the kernel, applications, system services, and AI workloads.

 - Define guardrails for how AI applications and agents access information, use sensors and tools, retain context, and act on a user’s behalf.

 - Lead threat modeling and architecture reviews across the platform, translating emerging threats into practical, enforceable requirements.

 - Prototype solutions, review security-critical systems code, and guide engineering teams through complex technical and product tradeoffs.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Deep experience designing or securing operating systems, kernels, embedded platforms, hypervisors, or other privileged systems software.

 - Complex understanding of operating system internals, including memory protection, process isolation, executable loading, device drivers, and privilege boundaries.

 - Experience building security architectures that span hardware, firmware, operating systems, applications, and cloud services.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Bring practical expertise in secure boot, code signing, device identity, attestation, trusted execution, and hardware-backed key protection.

 - Can write or review systems code in C, C++, Rust, or comparable languages, with a strong grasp of secure development and exploit mitigation.

 - Build rigorous threat models, influence cross-functional engineering teams, and communicate security tradeoffs clearly.

 - Care deeply about user privacy, personal agency, and building systems that earn trust through their design.


HELPFUL EXPERIENCE:

 - Shipping security technologies for consumer operating systems, mobile platforms, or connected devices.

 - Kernel hardening, memory-safety mitigations, virtualization-based security, or secure enclave integration.

 - Security architecture for AI agents, sensitive-context isolation, permissioned tool use, or prompt-injection resistance.

title: Technical Certification Lead
description:
About the Team

Customer Education helps customers build the practical skills and confidence to use AI and OpenAI products safely and effectively. We bring together customer insight, learning and enablement expertise, product signals, and measurement to help organizations move from access to durable adoption.

Within Customer Education, the Certification team helps individuals demonstrate competence for in-demand AI skills and helps customers and partners validate that their workforce has the skills they need to meet their AI-enabled business goals. Our work centers on the belief that learners should understand where to go to build skills and capabilities, how to demonstrate them, and what to pursue next. Similarly, Enterprise leaders should understand what each credential signifies and how it supports workforce readiness. We do this with transparency for the overall OpenAI credential framework and providing trusted, role-based certifications that verify practical capability.

About the Role

As Technical Certification Lead, you will lead the design, development, and ongoing quality of OpenAI’s technical role-based certifications. Your work will make clear what each certification validates and what candidates must demonstrate to earn it.

This is a hands-on people manager role on the Certification team. You will manage the Certification Assessment Specialists building technical assessments across the certification portfolio, setting priorities, coaching team members, and holding the team accountable for quality and delivery. You will personally turn shared certification frameworks into certification-specific competency models, job-task analyses, assessment blueprints, scoring rubrics, and passing criteria.

You will apply program-wide certification standards to individual technical certifications and partner with operations and platform teams to prepare assessments for delivery. You will align learning content to competency models and blueprints while keeping confidential assessment content separate from learning development.

You will take certifications from role analysis through pilot, launch readiness, and ongoing maintenance. As AI tools and technical roles evolve, you will keep the assessments relevant to the work people actually do.

Success means each certification makes a clear claim about what someone can do, the assessment supports that claim, and the curriculum gives candidates a practical way to build the skills they need.

In this role, you will:

 - Build and maintain competency models and facilitate job-task analyses for technical roles. Work with practitioners and subject matter experts (SMEs) to identify critical tasks, define the skills and proficiency each role requires, and keep the models current.

 - Define and maintain assessment blueprints and write scoring rubrics. Translate competencies into realistic tasks, define what evidence candidates must produce, and set clear criteria for evaluating performance in line with shared certification standards.

 - Lead standard-setting with subject matter experts and a psychometrician or measurement specialist, using a shared methodology to recommend the passing standard for each assessment.

 - Validate AI-assisted scoring against judgments from calibrated human reviewers. Define when scores require human review, and revalidate scoring after material changes to the model, assessment task, or rubric.

 - Manage and develop Certification Assessment Specialists across technical certifications. Set priorities, review their work, and guide the build and maintenance of assessment tasks, environments, evidence capture, and scoring workflows.

 - Secure and manage SME commitments for role analysis, task design, technical review, pilot feedback, and maintenance. Define what each expert is contributing and when it is needed.

 - Share competency models and permitted blueprint information with learning content developers, and review their content for alignment. Coordinate assessment and curriculum changes through the technical lead rather than direct sharing of confidential assessment details between assessment and learning teams.

 - Own ongoing assessment quality for each technical certification within shared program standards. Use pilot results, scoring consistency, technical reviews, and candidate feedback to identify issues. Partner with certification and measurement teams to calibrate rubrics and decide what needs updating or revalidation.

 - Provide technical input when candidates challenge an assessment task. Partner with operations to oversee fixes and validation for confirmed defects.

 - Define what credential holders must demonstrate to stay certified, when they must demonstrate it, and what evidence counts. Work with the team to align those requirements with shared standards, and with learning, platform, and operations teams to make appropriate renewal options available.

 - Make evidence-based readiness recommendations for pilots, launches, and updates. Document what has been tested, what risks remain, and which issues must be resolved before release. Coordinate technical handoff and delivery readiness with operations and platform teams.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have led the development and maintenance of role-based technical certifications or other high-stakes technical assessments, from role analysis through pilot, launch, and post-launch improvement.

 - Have directly managed and developed engineers or technical assessment specialists, including setting priorities, providing performance feedback, and improving the quality of the team’s work.

 - Have experience working at a technology company in a fast-paced environment, setting priorities and delivering work amid changing requirements and evolving business needs.

 - Have personally built competency models, facilitated job-task analyses, and used them to define assessment blueprints and write scoring rubrics.

 - Have designed hands-on assessments for software engineering, AI, cloud, or technical implementation roles, and can distinguish authentic evidence of capability from completion of a task.

 - Have built or validated AI-assisted scoring for assessments, with appropriate human review.

 - Have recruited and coordinated subject matter experts across teams, secured their time, and turned differing expert views into clear assessment decisions.

 - Have used evidence from pilots and live assessments to improve tasks and scoring, and can explain what would make you recommend a launch, a narrower pilot, or a delay.

 - Have worked with learning content developers to map curriculum and practice to competencies while maintaining the separation between preparation and assessment content.

 - Communicate technical and measurement tradeoffs clearly to engineers, learning teams, operations partners, and leaders.

 - Can review technical assessment work directly and coach others through design decisions without becoming the bottleneck.

 - Have maintained multiple technical assessments as products, tools, or job expectations changed, and know when to update or retire a task.

 - Care deeply about accessible assessments, consistent scoring, and making only the claims the evidence supports.

It’s a plus if you have experience:

 - Designing practical assessments for AI application development, agentic workflows, or customer-facing AI deployments.

 - Working with psychometricians on standard setting, rubric calibration, or validation of performance assessments.

 - Launching hands-on assessments across live and virtual delivery environments.

title: Strategy & Operations, Marketing & Creative - MBA
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Strategy & Operations, Marketing & Creative - MBA
Marketing & Creative shapes how customers discover Quince and how the brand shows up. We are seeking a Strategy & Operations Lead, Marketing & Creative to connect performance analytics with brand and creative strategy, helping grow our customer base efficiently. You will own growth initiatives, partner with creative teams on campaigns and content, and test what drives stronger acquisition, retention and conversion. Your work will turn insights into decisions about how we reach customers and where we invest. This role is based in our Palo Alto office, four days per week in office. The estimated start date will be June/July 2027. Candidates are welcome to apply to more than one Quince MBA role.
Strategy & Operations Leads help run the business inside their function. You will partner with senior leaders to set strategy, own initiatives end to end, and learn what it takes to build and scale a business inside a rapidly growing company.
A launchpad to entrepreneurship: operate as a core member of your team, roll up your sleeves and make an immediate, measurable impact across the business.
An accelerated growth path: work hand in hand with leaders across the company, take on a big scope, tackle complex problems and develop into a leader who knows how to build a business and grow a P&L.
Depth with purpose: own strategic initiatives that require you to go deep into the business. An obsession with the details is where the most meaningful breakthroughs come from.
Responsibilities
Own growth initiatives across paid, lifecycle/CRM and emerging channels
Analyze acquisition, retention and channel performance (CAC, ROAS, LTV) to guide budget and spend-mix decisions
Partner with creative teams on campaigns, content and brand strategy
Design and run tests to improve messaging, targeting and conversion
Work with merchandising on product launches and seasonal campaigns
Qualifications
Required:
3-6 years of prior professional experience in consulting, investment banking, private equity, tech, retail or related fields
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills
Ability to operate in ambiguity and bring structure to new problem sets
Comfort in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment
Comfort with marketing analytics and experimentation
Preferred:
Experience in growth or brand marketing, e-commerce or consumer tech
Direct-to-consumer or retail background
Interest in creative strategy and brand building
Pay Range: $175,000 - 200,000
All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location.   Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.
WHY QUINCE?
Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

The engineer will leverage RCAR principles, collision repair industry practices, organizational feedback, and service engineering expertise to influence design concepts before key architecture and component decisions are finalized. The role will simplify repair strategies for complex vehicle structures, establish repair-versus-replace recommendations, create service part numbers and if necessary drawings for service unique subassemblies, and own the service bill of materials to enable sourcing for our NPI stakeholders. This position partners closely with Vehicle Engineering, Design, Service NPI, Manufacturing, Quality, Purchasing, Supply Chain, Technical Publications, Collision R&D, Service Operations, Insurance, and certified collision repair facilities in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment. Responsibilities Lead collision repairability assessments for exterior systems and components beginning in concept, architecture, and advanced development phases and continuing through production launch. Evaluate repairability and replacement strategies for body sheet metal, including closures, fenders, quarter panels, body sides, bumper reinforcements, underbody exterior panels, and related structural or cosmetic assemblies. Translate collision repair requirements into clear design inputs, serviceability targets, and trade-off recommendations for Engineering and Design teams. Establish repair-versus-replace strategies that consider technician safety, repair quality, vehicle performance, customer experience, cycle time, parts availability and total repair cost. Apply RCAR standards and principles, along with recognized collision repair practices, to drive service-focused design concepts and improve vehicle insurability. Represent the voice of the technician and customer in design reviews, architecture decisions, development milestone reviews, prototype evaluations, and production readiness activities. Identify complex vehicle structure systems that may create repair challenges and develop simplified, repeatable, and clearly documented repair paths. Define permissible repair methods, limitations, sectioning or replacement boundaries, attachment strategies, joining requirements, corrosion protection, sealing, refinishing, and post-repair verification needs. Assess the impact of mixed materials, adhesives, rivets, welds, fasteners, composites, castings, high-strength steels, aluminum, and other joining or material technologies on collision repair. With the support of engineering define required tools, fixtures, equipment, and consumables for certified collision repair facilities. Participate in hands-on and virtual prototype, pilot, and validation repairs to confirm that proposed repair strategies can be executed safely, consistently, and efficiently in the field. Create and maintain service part numbers for collision-related components, subassemblies, kits, hardware, consumables, and repair-specific parts in the appropriate product lifecycle and service systems. Own the collision repair service bill of materials for new product introduction, ensuring accurate structure, applicability, service intent, supersession logic, interchangeability, and release status. Ensure service BOMs remain aligned with the latest production design, engineering changes, supplier changes, and approved repair strategies through disciplined change management. Define service assembly content and replacement packages where a repair is not technically, economically, or operationally appropriate at the individual component level. Partner with Technical Publications to convert engineering decisions into collision repair procedures, illustrations, labor-impact inputs, parts recommendations, training content, and technical communications. Coordinate field returns, repair observations, and part analysis to validate assumptions and improve future product designs. Support launch readiness, service introduction, repair network readiness, and field actions related to collision repairability and service parts. Build and maintain standards, playbooks, checklists, and design review tools that institutionalize prediction, prevention, and protection across vehicle programs. Drive change management activities by evaluating service impact, repair strategy, part interchangeability, documentation updates, and disposition of affected service content. Technical collision repair training, I-CAR training, OEM certification, ASE certification, or equivalent industry credentials are valued. Training or demonstrated proficiency in CAD, PLM, BOM management, technical documentation, or engineering change control is preferred. 8+ years of experience in collision repair, automotive service engineering, body repair, vehicle body structures, repair facility operations, estimating, insurance claims, or a closely related field. Strong understanding of repair-versus-replace decision-making and the factors that influence vehicle insurability, repair cost, cycle time, safety, and customer experience. Experience interpreting engineering drawings, CAD data, service procedures, parts catalogs, or repair manuals. Experience working with part numbering, bills of material, engineering change management, or product lifecycle management systems. Knowledge of automotive materials and joining methods, including steel, aluminum, plastics, composites, adhesives, rivets, welds, and mechanical fasteners. Ability to identify risks in complex vehicle structures and communicate clear, actionable recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Strong written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to influence design decisions across a cross-functional organization. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple programs, deliverables, and priorities across development phases and locations. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, especially when requirements are incomplete, ambiguous, or technically complex. Experience with CATIA or comparable CAD tools; ability to review and communicate from 3D data. Experience with EV architecture, high-voltage vehicle safety, ADAS-related repair considerations, calibration requirements, and post-repair validation. Join Our Team as an Lean Engineer III!
The Lean Engineer III leads continuous improvement initiatives within assigned value streams to improve process capability, productivity, quality, flow, and operational performance. While applying Lean manufacturing principles, Six Sigma methodologies, and data-driven problem solving, this role analyzes and improves production systems, eliminates waste and variability, and implements sustainable process improvements that support business and manufacturing objectives.
The Lean Engineer III works cross-functionally with operations and functional teams, leads high-impact improvement projects, establishes effective production and problem-solving standards, and builds team capability through coaching and application of continuous improvement practices. This role uses strong analytical, technical, and influencing skills to identify improvement opportunities, facilitate problem solving, and sustain measurable results across manufacturing operations.
Key Responsibilities:
Lean & Six Sigma Improvement Execution: Lead and execute Lean and Six Sigma initiatives within assigned value streams, applying continuous improvement methodologies to improve productivity, quality, process capability, flow, and waste reduction in alignment with operational and business objectives.
Project Leadership & Delivery: Lead cross-functional improvement projects of moderate to high complexity, establishing objectives, coordinating activities, managing implementation, and ensuring measurable improvements are integrated into standard work and sustained over time.
Process Improvement & Problem Solving: Evaluate manufacturing and support processes to identify waste, variation, bottlenecks, and performance gaps; apply structured problem-solving methodologies to determine root causes and implement improvements in quality, cost, flow, and process capability.
Lean & Six Sigma Methodology Application: Apply appropriate Lean and Six Sigma methods, including DMAIC, Value Stream Mapping (VSM), Kaizen, 5S, Kanban, Standard Work, visual management, and Root Cause Analysis to improve process performance and operational effectiveness.
Data Analysis & Performance Management: Analyze process and performance data using statistical methods to identify trends, prioritize improvement opportunities, validate results, and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs); communicate actionable findings and recommendations to operational and functional leaders.
Change Management & Sustainment: Partner with leaders and operational teams to implement process changes, build stakeholder ownership, and integrate improvements into standard operating procedures, work instructions, visual management, and other operating systems to support adoption and sustainment.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Influence:  Collaborate with Operations, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders to align improvement priorities, resolve barriers, coordinate implementation, and deliver sustainable results through effective influence without direct authority.
Continuous Improvement Capability Building: Coach project teams and operational stakeholders in structured problem solving and the effective application of Lean and Six Sigma methodologies to strengthen continuous improvement capabilities and reinforce process discipline.
Standardization & Governance: Support consistent application of Lean and Six Sigma methods, standards, and governance within assigned areas, ensuring improvement activities align with enterprise continuous improvement frameworks and local operating requirements.

Identify gaps in business metrics and then work with all levels of the factory value stream in establishing and executing a strategy for improving them
Assess using Value Stream Mapping and root cause problem solving tools (such as A3, 5 Whys, Fishbone Diagram, etc) the current state of the value stream Operations, develop Future State vision and drive and monitor the implementation plan
Develops Lean capability across the value stream by coaching value stream staff, front‑line leaders, and associates in lean principles, strengthening problem‑solving behaviors, operational discipline, and a culture of continuous improvement.

Perform time studies of the operations with the goal of re-balancing the operation and eliminating waste.
Modify/update physical and digital layouts as required during the transformation of the site.
Ensure process owner involvement in Standardized Work development and team leadership
Use kaizen funnel tracking and reporting systems to build detailed project plans, drive performance, and ensure transformational and continuous improvement projects finish on time and deliver their goals.
Collaborate with leadership to develop a Lean value stream Transformation Roadmap, driving breakthrough or Best-in-class performance that balances resources between internal plant efficiency and external customer-focused effectiveness projects through “Just Do It” improvements, Kaizens, and Workshops.
Partners with values stream Management team to identify systemic barriers to project success and strategically drive the organizational, process, and behavioral changes required to remove them.
Document improvement process learning and shares best practices throughout the company
Identifies and brings forward to value stream team new project opportunities
Partners with the values stream Manager on strategic initiatives that strengthen standards compliance, accelerate the deployment of new systems, and shape innovative, future‑focused solutions that drive sustainable operational excellence across the value stream.

Crafting the world’s finest coffee, one meaningful moment at a time
We believe in creating a warm and welcoming space where every cup of coffee sparks connection.   As a coffeehouse leader, you don’t just run a business—you lead a team that creates moments of connection and joy.    Every day provides an opportunity to lead with craft and heart, making your coffeehouse a place where your community feels welcome.
We are invested in your growth journey, empowered through developmental experiences as well as our industry leading benefits .
We'd love to hear from people with:
3 years retail / customer service management experience or 4+ years of US Military service
Strong organizational, interpersonal and problem solving skills
Entrepreneurial mentality with experience in a sales focused environment
Strong leadership skills and the ability to coach and mentor team partners with professional maturity
Minimum High School or GED
Requirements:
Legal documentation establishing your identity and eligibility to be legally employed in the country in which you apply.
Ability to work full time (the work regularly demands in excess of 40 hours per week) including variable hours including early mornings, evenings, weekends and/ or holidays.
Let us give you the opportunity to grow as an individual, to build lasting relationships and make an impact in a place where people, quality and value mean everything.
Join us and connect with something bigger, apply today!
As a Starbucks partner, you (and your family) will have access to medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, and other voluntary insurance benefits. Partners have access to short-term and long-term disability, paid parental leave, family expansion reimbursement, paid vacation from date of hire*, sick time (accrued at 1 hour for every 25 hours worked), eight paid holidays, and two personal days per year. Starbucks also offers eligible partners participation in a 401(k) retirement plan with employer match, a discounted company stock program (S.I.P.), Starbucks equity program (Bean Stock), incentivized emergency savings, and financial well-being tools.  Additionally, Starbucks offers 100% upfront tuition coverage for a first-time bachelor’s degree through Arizona State University’s online program via the Starbucks College Achievement Plan, student loan management resources, and access to other educational opportunities.  You will also have access to backup care and DACA reimbursement.   Starbucks will comply with any applicable state and local laws regarding employee leave benefits, including, but not limited to providing time off pursuant to the Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, and in accordance with its plans and policies. This list is subject to change depending on collective bargaining in locations where partners have a certified bargaining representative. For additional information regarding partner perks and more detailed information about benefits, go to starbucksbenefits.com .
*If you are working in CA, CO, IL, LA, ME, MA, NE, ND or RI, you will accrue vacation up to a maximum of 120 hours (190 in CA) for roles below director and 200 hours (316 in CA) for roles at director or above.  For roles in other states, you will be granted vacation time starting at 120 hours annually for roles below director and 200 hours annually for roles director and above.
The actual base pay offered to the successful candidate will be based on multiple factors, including but not limited to job-related knowledge/skills, experience, geographical location, and internal equity.  At Starbucks, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at the high end of the range for their role, and compensation decisions are dependent upon the facts and circumstances of each position and candidate.
Starbucks Coffee Company is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Qualified applicants with criminal histories will be considered for employment in a manner consistent with all federal, state and local ordinances.
Starbucks Coffee Company is committed to offering reasonable accommodations to job applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact us at applicantaccommodation@starbucks.com or 1(888) 611-2258.

location: San Francisco, New York, Seattle, Chicago, Atlanta, Remote in the US
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies — from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups — use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Stripe Marketing organization is undergoing a fundamental transformation in how it works. We're building a team of Forward Deployed AI Accelerators (FDAs) embedded directly with marketing cohorts to make AI the default mode for all work — not an occasional tool, but the foundation of how every marketer at Stripe executes.
Today, marketers are already achieving remarkable results — building their own data dashboards, creating agents that compress multi-day processes, and authoring tools that accelerate workflows. The FDA team exists to take what's working and systematically scale it across the entire marketing organization.
What you'll do
As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, you'll be embedded with a cohort of 25–45 marketers organized by functional team, shared workflow, or location. You'll build alongside them, and you'll help them fundamentally change how they operate. Your measure of success is the number of workflows you've permanently transformed and the extent to which those in your cohort start any task with an AI tool.
Responsibilities
Identify and document the highest-leverage workflow transformations within your cohort's day-to-day work by deeply understanding their processes and outputs
Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to each marketer's specific responsibilities
Coach and partner with each marketer through a progressive journey — from awareness, to first win, to regular AI integration, to full workflow transformation, to self-sufficiency
Teach marketers to build and iterate on their own tools over time, creating independence
Recognize patterns across your cohort and systematically scale what works — a tool built for one marketer will be reusable for their peers
Document every tool, playbook, and transformation pattern you build so the entire FDA team uses each other's work
Share wins visibly within your cohort and with leadership to build momentum, inspire, and celebrate success
Track individual and cohort progress rigorously against a defined maturity model, moving every marketer toward self-sustaining, AI-first work
Prepare marketers for an agentic future — not just prompt writing, but designing, building, and overseeing autonomous, multi-agent workflows
Who you are
We're looking for people who have already lived the transformation they'll be driving for others. You've used AI to fundamentally change how work gets done, not as a novelty, but as your default operating mode.
You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support.
You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide.
You understand marketing work. You either have direct experience in marketing or quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of your assigned cohort. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, adapt your style to different people, and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You are high-caliber, persistent, and versatile. Your skills and experience are valuable across the company. You're the kind of person who succeeds in many roles at Stripe.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next quarter.

Track record of coaching, teaching, or enabling others, with evidence that people you've helped actually changed how they work

Experience in a formal AI transformation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hands-on builds
Experience helping people become more expert AI users and capable builders
Experience in marketing, marketing operations, growth, or a closely adjacent function, including familiarity with marketing technology stacks (e.g., Marketo, Salesforce, analytics platforms, content management tools)

We are seeking a Senior Treasury Specialist to oversee capital adequacy, liquidity stress testing, financial risk management, and contingency funding planning for Bridge National Trust Bank (BNTB)'s Treasury and Reserve Operations. Issuing digital assets that are fully backed by reserves raises new questions for a regulated bank: how much capital and liquidity it needs, how it holds up under stress, and how it shows management, the Board, and regulators that it is safe and sound.

In this role, you will support Stripe’s proposed national trust bank, Bridge National Trust Bank (BNTB), currently in formation and subject to full regulatory approval by the OCC. You will build and run the bank's capital, liquidity, and financial risk management framework and the governance around it. That includes the analysis, monitoring, policies, and reporting that let the bank grow safely as regulatory requirements for stablecoin issuers continue to evolve.
You will partner closely with the BNTB Treasury and Reserve Operations team, the broader Bridge and Stripe treasury team, risk, compliance, finance, accounting, regulatory reporting, product, data science, and engineering. In the near term, you will help design the frameworks and put the first cycles into practice. As the bank scales, you will turn them into repeatable, automated processes.
Responsibilities
Own capital planning and the ongoing assessment of the bank's capital adequacy
Own and report on capital, liquidity, and financial risk metrics against risk appetite and limits; escalate breaches and emerging trends
Design and run liquidity and capital stress testing, and turn the results into recommendations for funding and capital strategy
Own contingency funding planning, including annual testing and tracking remediation to closure
Maintain treasury risk policies and procedures, and prepare management and Board reporting
Provide risk oversight of reserve and investment activity (counterparty, concentration, liquidity and interest rate risk); partner with product, data science, and engineering to automate monitoring and reporting
Coordinate with the broader Stripe treasury team on capital management initiatives including consolidated capital planning, infrastructure and methodology development and governance frameworks
Who you are
You are a builder - we are building a new OCC  chartered bank and we are looking for folks who thrive in a fast-paced, growing environment. This means one day you may be working on a stress testing methodology and the next day speaking with engineers about a critical liquidity concept to be incorporated into systems. You will thrive here if that energizes you, if you take ownership of whatever is needed, and if you bring the same rigor to a stress test assumption as you do to a Board memo. You combine the discipline of a risk manager with the instincts of a builder, and you can explain capital and liquidity concepts clearly to treasury, product, and engineering partners.

7-10 years of experience in treasury, capital planning, liquidity risk, stress testing, or financial risk management
Hands-on experience building or running capital or liquidity frameworks at a regulated US financial institution
Experience writing and presenting on policies, procedures, or management and Board materials
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to assess incomplete information and make sound recommendations
Strong experience using AI tools to build, automate, and improve workflows and data analytics
Strong communication skills and the ability to build relationships across treasury, risk, finance, product, and engineering

Interest rate or fixed-income risk analytics
Experience with SQL, Python, or equivalent for analysis and reporting
